# Components

Grouped by category (src/components/categories.ts). Each category is a subpath: `import { Chip } from "hadi-march/actions"`; `hadi-march/ui` re-exports every component.

### Layout — `hadi-march/layout`

| Component | Status | What | Composed of |
|---|---|---|---|
| Accordion | stable | Stacked sections that open one at a time or several together: animated height, ↑ ↓ Home End between headers, separated or contained look. | [ListRow](#listrow), [Chevron](#chevron) |
| AppShell | stable | The application frame: a sidebar column and the main area with optional banner and sticky header; a skip link; full width on narrow screens. | [Layout](#layout) |
| BottomRightControls | stable | One fixed page corner (bottom, end side; mirrors in RTL) that page-wide controls put themselves into, in order, instead of overlapping. | — |
| DevicePreview | experimental | Content as on a real phone or tablet: device body, notch, status bar, home indicator, real screen size, rotation; the mouse acts as a finger (drag to scroll, fling, long press). | [OverlayScope](#overlayscope) |
| Disclosure | stable | A collapsible section on native details / summary: keyboard and screen reader support built in, animated open and close. | [Chevron](#chevron) |
| ExplodedView | experimental | Takes its content apart like an exploded drawing and puts it back: the same elements tilt and rise as plates with name tags (chosen parts), or one element opens into its shadow, surface, content and focus ring. | — |
| Grid | stable | Responsive grid that never overflows: fixed or automatic columns, fill or balance the last row, equal row heights; pure CSS. | — |
| Layout | stable | The frame all pages of an app share: content plus the page corner (BottomRightControls) with its back-to-top button; Page builds on it. | [Button](#button), [Badge](#badge), [Progress](#progress), [ScrollToTop](#scrolltotop) |
| OverlayScope | stable | A box that keeps the layers opened inside it (drawers, dialogs, menus, toasts) inside it: previews, device frames, panels, demos. | — |
| PanelHeader | experimental | The bar on top of (or under) a panel: lead, icon, title, subtitle, count, actions and a close button; sizes, divider, sticky, muted tone; usable as a drag handle. | [IconButton](#iconbutton) |
| ResizeHandle | experimental | The ready element of the resize-handle behavior: a strip on an edge or corner with one look (line, grip, colour); full separator with value + set, or a bare grip for an own gesture. | — |
| Spacer | stable | A flexible gap in a row that pushes the following items to the end. | — |
| Splitter | stable | Two resizable panes: drag the handle or use the arrow keys (mirrored in RTL), Home / End, Enter resets. | [ResizeHandle](#resizehandle) |
| Stack | stable | Layout primitives: Stack (a row or column with token gaps and alignment), Toolbar (a labelled bar of controls), Divider (a rule, labelled or vertical). | — |
| StatusBar | experimental | Bottom strip of an editor or app: start / end items, text or buttons (actions or command ids), tones with a breathing busy dot, live announcements, low-priority items to a … menu when narrow. | [ListRow](#listrow), [Menu](#menu), [Tooltip](#tooltip), [StatusDot](#statusdot) |
| Window | stable | A movable, resizable window inside its area: dock to an edge, minimize, fill, close; Windows, Mac or HADİ look. | [PanelHeader](#panelheader), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [ResizeHandle](#resizehandle) |

### Typography — `hadi-march/typography`

| Component | Status | What | Composed of |
|---|---|---|---|
| ClampText | experimental | Text folded to N lines with a "more" / "less" switch shown only when it does not fit; controlled or not, own texts, fold only. | [Button](#button) |
| CodeView | stable | Read-only code block: line numbers, syntax colours (js/ts/jsx/tsx, css, html, json, sh), wrap toggle and a copy button. | [CopyButton](#copybutton), [Button](#button), [PanelHeader](#panelheader) |
| Kbd | stable | Keyboard key: text, or a shortcut string (mod+k) written for the platform (Ctrl+K, ⌘K). | — |
| OverflowText | stable | Text that scrolls only when it does not fit: hover, focus, always or while visible; bounce, loop or once; RTL-aware fade; Marquee is the endless ticker. | — |
| SectionLabel | experimental | The small heading of a group inside a panel (menu, palette, sidebar, property grid): uppercase and faint, with an icon, a count and an actions slot. | — |

### Actions — `hadi-march/actions`

| Component | Status | What | Composed of |
|---|---|---|---|
| Button | stable | Button in six variants (one a link-like text button) and three sizes with icons, loading (locks and spins), a pressed toggle state, pill shape, router links (href) and block width; ActionButton draws an action() or a plain { label, run } with its guard, confirm and toasts. | [Spinner](#spinner) |
| ButtonGroup | stable | Groups related buttons (role=group with a label), spaced or attached into one segmented strip; RTL keeps the rounded ends outside. | — |
| Chevron | experimental | The arrow that turns when something opens: four directions, mirrored in RTL, follows the nearest aria-expanded ancestor or an `open` prop; own icon, smooth / spring / no motion. | — |
| Chip | stable | Label pill: static, toggle (filter, aria-pressed) or removable; long labels scroll with OverflowText. | [OverflowText](#overflowtext), [IconButton](#iconbutton) |
| CopyButton | stable | Copies text to the clipboard: a text or icon-only button that confirms (Copied) for a moment and reports failure with a toast. | [Button](#button), [IconButton](#iconbutton) |
| IconButton | stable | Icon-only button: the label is required and becomes its accessible name and title; four sizes, danger / solid / raised variants, round shape, a pressed toggle state, an inverse look for dark media, and href to draw a link. | — |
| MadeWithMarch | stable | Optional credit line "Developed with March and 💗": text, badge or small; the link is one constant (MARCH_URL). | — |
| Menu | stable | Trigger button with a floating menu of items, links and action()s (separators, shortcuts, danger, permissions) and the full menu keyboard model; Dropdown floats any content. | [Button](#button), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Popover](#popover), [ListRow](#listrow), [CheckMark](#checkmark), [Kbd](#kbd), Divider |
| OverflowToolbar | experimental | Toolbar whose items that do not fit go to a More menu (lowest priority first); command ids from the Command manager, toggles, separators, roving focus. | [Button](#button), [IconButton](#iconbutton), Divider, [Menu](#menu), [Tooltip](#tooltip) |
| ScrollToTop | stable | Back-to-top button: shows after the page is scrolled down, scrolls back on the motion engine; puts itself into BottomRightControls. | [IconButton](#iconbutton), [BottomRightControls](#bottomrightcontrols) |
| UndoRedo | experimental | The undo / redo button pair of an editor (IconButtons): fed by an undo stack or four props; the tooltip names the step and the shortcut. | [IconButton](#iconbutton) |

### Feedback — `hadi-march/feedback`

| Component | Status | What | Composed of |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alert | stable | A message in one of five tones (info, success, warn, danger, neutral) with an optional title, icon and dismiss button; Notice is an alias. | [IconButton](#iconbutton) |
| CheckMark | experimental | The yes / no / partly mark (✓ ✕ –) with its accessible text: plain, soft or solid disc, own glyphs and texts, colour from the value or a token, and a transition when the value changes (flip, fade, pop, draw or your own). | — |
| Empty | stable | Empty state: an icon, a title, a line of text and the next step (actions), so an empty screen says what to do. | [IconTile](#icontile) |
| ErrorBox | stable | What went wrong, in words (an Error, a message or any value), with an optional title and a retry button. | [Alert](#alert), [Button](#button) |
| LiveStatus | experimental | A polite live region that says what changed (a count, a range, a move): shown as text or only read, with an optional hint line before it. | — |
| Loader | stable | A full-area loading state (a large spinner and a line of text), inline or over its container; bootLoader hides the static boot screen. | [Spinner](#spinner) |
| Progress | stable | A progress bar: a value or indeterminate, tones, three sizes, a label with the percentage; brand colours as a gradient, segments or a flowing cycle; a thin line driven from outside, and equal parts with a timed fill. | — |
| PullToRefresh | experimental | Pull a scroll area down (touch or mouse) past a threshold to run an async refresh; spinning indicator, keyboard button, live status. | [Button](#button) |
| Skeleton | stable | Placeholder lines or a block in the shape of the content on its way, so nothing jumps when it arrives; brand or single-colour shimmer. | — |
| Spinner | stable | A turning ring while something loads: three sizes, one colour or the theme's several (brand), an accessible label. | — |
| StatusDot | experimental | A small dot in a tone or theme colour, still or pulsing (ring / blink); an image with a label, decoration without one. | — |

## Accordion

Stacked sections with a header button each. By default opening one closes the others; `multiple` lets several stay open. The panel height animates, ↑ ↓ Home End move between headers, and closed panels are inert. Headers can carry an icon and a subtitle; `variant="contained"` draws one framed list instead of separate cards.

Composed of: [ListRow](#listrow), [Chevron](#chevron)

```tsx
<Accordion multiple open={[0]} items={[
  { title: "Shipping", subtitle: "2–3 days", content: <Shipping /> },
  { title: "Returns", content: <Returns /> },
]} />
```

Full page: src/components/layout/accordion/docs.md

## ActivityBar

The narrow icon bar at the edge of an editor that switches the side view (files, search, source control…). An indicator glides to the active view; choosing the active view again collapses the side view (`value` becomes `null`). Items can carry count badges, sit at the far end (settings, account) or be plain actions. Vertical or horizontal (a bottom bar on phones), and mirrored in RTL.

Composed of: [Tabs](#tabs), [Badge](#badge), [Tooltip](#tooltip)

```tsx
<ActivityBar value={$view} onChange={(v) => $view = v} controls="side-view" items={[
  { id: "files", label: "Files", icon: files, shortcut: "mod+shift+e" },
  { id: "search", label: "Search", icon: search, badge: () => $hits },
  { id: "settings", label: "Settings", icon: settings, position: "end", onSelect: openSettings },
]} />
```

Full page: src/components/navigation/activity-bar/docs.md

## Alert

A message that stays on the page: a tone (`info`, `success`, `warn`, `danger`, `neutral`), an optional bold title, the tone's icon (or your own) and an optional dismiss button. `Notice` is the same component.

Composed of: [IconButton](#iconbutton)

```tsx
<Alert tone="warn" title="Quota" dismissable onDismiss={() => track("quota")}>90% of the storage is used this month.</Alert>
```

Full page: src/components/feedback/alert/docs.md

## AppShell

The application frame. Desktop: a sticky sidebar column (usually a NavMenu or NavSidebar) and a scrolling main area; above the main column an optional banner slot (`top`, for update or offline banners) and a sticky header (`header`, for the title, search and user menu). Narrow screens: a slim top bar with the menu button and a full-width main. A "Skip to content" link comes first. It is its own module, so an app's entry does not pull in page scaffolding.

Composed of: [Layout](#layout)

```tsx
<AppShell nav={<NavMenu items={items} />} top={<UpdateBanner />} header={<PageTitle />}>
  <Outlet />
</AppShell>
```

Full page: src/components/layout/app-shell/docs.md

## AppUI

march-app-ui, the core of March IDE and the base of an IDE shell: a top bar (a title, your tools and the **Layout** menu), a side slot (an ActivityBar), the [DockLayout](#docklayout) workspace and a status slot (a StatusBar). The Layout menu lists the presets, the saved layouts ("Save this layout"), every panel (checked when it is open; choosing one opens or collapses it), "Open all panels" and "Reset to default". Colours come from the page's theme and accent. Activity bars, status bars and editors are built on top of it.

Composed of: [DockLayout](#docklayout), [Menu](#menu)

```tsx
<AppUI title="march-app-ui" panels={panels} presets={{
  default: { title: "Default", tree: () => row([.24, tabs("files")], [.76, col([.7, tabs("editor")], [.3, tabs("console")])]) },
  code: { title: "Code", tree: () => row([.2, tabs("files", { collapsed: true })], [.8, tabs(["editor", "console"])]) },
}} persist="my-ide" tools={<Button>Run</Button>} />
```

Full page: src/components/composite/app-ui/docs.md

## Avatar

A person's picture. Without an image (or when it fails to load) it shows the initials of the name on a colour taken from the name, so the same person always has the same colour. Every part is yours: a ready text or an icon instead of the initials, a fixed theme colour, the shape and the accessible name.

```tsx
<Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" src={url} size="lg" />
<Avatar name="Linus Torvalds" color="brand-orange" shape="square" />
<Avatar text="+3" color="neutral" />
<Avatar icon={user} label="Guest" />
```

Full page: src/components/social/avatar/docs.md

## AvatarGroup

A row of overlapping avatars for the people of a thing (attendees, members, readers). The ones that do not fit become a "+N" bubble. The bubble, the spacing, the colour and the shape are yours.

Composed of: [Avatar](#avatar)

```tsx
<AvatarGroup names={["Ada", "Linus", "Grace", "Alan", "Margaret"]} max={4} />
<AvatarGroup names={[{ name: "Ada", src: url }, "Linus"]} spacing="gap" shape="square" more={(n) => <b>{n}+</b>} />
```

Full page: src/components/social/avatar-group/docs.md

## Badge

A small label: a status in a tone, a dot badge (a coloured dot before the text, still or pulsing) or a count badge. Count badges hide at 0 (unless `showZero`), cap at `max` ("99+") and can carry an accessible label ("3 unread").

Composed of: [StatusDot](#statusdot)

```tsx
<Badge tone="success">Active</Badge>
<Badge tone="warn" dot>Pending</Badge>
<Badge count={unread} label="unread" />
```

Full page: src/components/data/badge/docs.md

## BeforeAfter

A before / after comparison: two layers on top of each other and a divider between them. Drag anywhere on the area (a press jumps the divider there), move the handle with the keyboard, or set `follow` so the divider tracks the mouse without a press. Horizontal or vertical; the horizontal one is mirrored in right-to-left text. The first time it scrolls into view the divider sways once, so it reads as something to move.

Composed of: [Badge](#badge)

```tsx
<BeforeAfter before={<img src="old.png" alt="" />} after={<img src="new.png" alt="" />} beforeLabel="Before" afterLabel="After" />
<BeforeAfter orientation="vertical" follow ratio="4 / 3" before={…} after={…} />
<BeforeAfter value={$pos} onChange={(v) => $pos.set(v)} before={…} after={…} />
<BeforeAfter grip={<Icon of={heart} />} step={5} valueText={(v) => `${v} percent of the old design`} before={…} after={…} />
<BeforeAfter grip={false} hint={false} before={…} after={…} />   // the line only, no sway
```

Full page: src/components/landing/before-after/docs.md

## BottomNav

The mobile tab bar: a colored bubble slides to the active tab, tabs carry count or dot badges, and an optional raised Create button in the middle wears a slowly turning ring of the four HADİ colors (Heyecan, Aktivite, Dostluk, İletişim).

Composed of: [Badge](#badge), [OverflowText](#overflowtext), [ListRow](#listrow), [Drawer](#drawer)

```tsx
<BottomNav items={tabs} value={$tab} onChange={(id) => $tab = id} onCreate={compose} />
```

Full page: src/components/composite/bottom-nav/docs.md

## BottomRightControls

Four fixed page corners — `top-start`, `top-end`, `bottom-start`, `bottom-end` (start/end mirror in RTL) — that page-wide controls put themselves into: back to top, a chat bubble, a feedback button, a connection badge. Controls do not each pick a fixed position and overlap: they stack in their corner in `order`. `BottomRightControls` is the bottom-end corner. Inside a Layout use `useLayout().add(corner, node)` or the `corners` prop.

```tsx
import { addCornerControl, BottomRightControls, CornerControls } from "hadi-march/layout";

const off = addCornerControl("bottom-end", <button>Geri bildirim</button>, 10)  // lower order = nearer the edge
off()                                                                           // also on component cleanup
<CornerControls corner="top-end" />   // render a corner yourself (else it is made on first use)
```

Full page: src/components/layout/bottom-right-controls/docs.md

## BranchingStory

A choose-your-own-path story. Every passage ends in choices; the reader's path collects as a trail at the top (any step rewinds the story to it) and the endings found so far are counted. A pick lights the chosen button, fades the others and turns the page: the new passage swings in from the reading direction, from the other side when going back, and mirrored in right-to-left text. Keys 1–9 pick a choice.

Composed of: [Badge](#badge), [Breadcrumbs](#breadcrumbs), [Button](#button), [Kbd](#kbd), [ListRow](#listrow)

```tsx
<BranchingStory start="intro" action={<Button>Join</Button>} passages={{
  intro: { title: "Saturday morning", body: "…", choices: [{ label: "Look around", to: "explore" }, { label: "Host", to: "host", note: "a few steps" }] },
  explore: { body: "…", choices: [{ label: "The run", to: "friends" }] },
  friends: { title: "New friends", body: "…", ending: "Social butterfly" },
}} />
<BranchingStory start="intro" passages={…} transition="slide" keys={false}
  labels={{ start: "Home", restart: "Once more", endings: (found, total) => `${found} of ${total} endings` }}
  renderChoice={(choice, i) => <b>{i + 1}. {choice.label}</b>} />
<BranchingStory start="intro" passages={…} restart={false} trail={false} transition={(side) => ({
  leave: { opacity: [1, 0], transform: ["scale(1)", "scale(.9)"] },
  enter: { opacity: [0, 1], transform: [`translateY(${40 * side}px)`, "translateY(0px)"] }, duration: 500 })} />
```

Full page: src/components/landing/branching-story/docs.md

## Breadcrumbs

A path bar (folder › file › symbol). A crumb is a link (`href`), a button (`onSelect`) or, with `siblings`, a menu of the items beside it — jump to another file of the same folder. When the path does not fit, the middle crumbs collapse into a "…" menu; the first and the last always stay. Separators follow the reading direction.

Composed of: [Button](#button), [Menu](#menu), [OverflowText](#overflowtext)

```tsx
<Breadcrumbs label="File path" items={[
  { id: "hadi", label: "hadi", icon: folder, onSelect: () => openFolder("hadi") },
  { id: "src", label: "src", icon: folder, siblings: () => folders("hadi") },
  { id: "file", label: "app.ts", icon: fileText },
]} />
```

Full page: src/components/navigation/breadcrumbs/docs.md

## Button

The button. Six variants (`primary` is the theme's orange fill, `secondary` the default, `ghost`, `danger`, `dark` ink fill, `link` text that reads as a link and flows inline), three sizes, a leading or trailing icon, `loading` (locks the button and shows a spinner instead of the icon), `block` width, `shape="pill"`, `pressed` (a toggle button) and `href` (renders a router link styled as a button).

Composed of: [Spinner](#spinner)

```tsx
<Button variant="primary" icon={plus}>New project</Button>
<Button loading={$saving} on:click={save}>Save</Button>
<Button href="/docs" iconEnd={arrowRight}>Docs</Button>
<ActionButton action={remove} args={[row]} />
<Button loading={$saving} spinner={false} icon={save}>Save</Button>   // no spinner: the icon stays
<Button loading={$saving} spinner={<MyDots />}>Save</Button>          // your own busy mark
<p>3 comments. <Button variant="link" on:click={showAll}>View all</Button></p>   // inline text button
<Button variant="ghost" pressed={$wrap} on:click={() => { $wrap = !$wrap }}>Wrap</Button>   // toggle: aria-pressed + pressed look
<Button variant="primary" shape="pill" icon={arrowUp}>12 new posts</Button>
<ActionButton action={{ label: "Archive", run: archive }} args={[row]} role="menuitem" />   // a plain action; other attributes go to the button
```

Full page: src/components/actions/button/docs.md

## ButtonGroup

Related buttons side by side: spaced (the default) or `attached` into one strip whose outer ends are rounded. The group has `role="group"` and a label, so screen readers announce what the buttons belong to.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup attached label="Alignment">
  <Button>Start</Button><Button>Center</Button><Button>End</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

Full page: src/components/actions/button-group/docs.md

## Calendar

A month grid. Dates are plain ISO strings (`"2026-03-14"`) and the arithmetic runs in UTC, so a daylight-saving change never shifts a day. The first weekday and the names come from the locale; days outside `min` / `max` or matched by `isDisabled` cannot be picked; `rangeFrom` / `rangeTo` highlight a range.

Composed of: [PeriodNav](#periodnav)

```tsx
<Calendar bind:value={$day} min="2026-03-10" max="2026-04-20" />
<Calendar value={$from} rangeFrom={$from} rangeTo={$to} isDisabled={(iso) => holidays.has(iso)} />
```

Full page: src/components/forms/calendar/docs.md

## Card

A surface for one piece of content: an optional header with a title, a subtitle and actions, the body, and an optional footer. `action()` objects in `actions` render as buttons that run, confirm and report the action.

Composed of: [PanelHeader](#panelheader)

```tsx
<Card title="HADİ" subtitle="Business plan" actions={[edit]} footer={<span>Updated today</span>}>…</Card>
<Card flush>…</Card>
<Card as="article" plain>…</Card>
```

Full page: src/components/data/card/docs.md

## Carousel

A row of slides that scrolls and snaps: one to four per view on wide screens (a slide and a peek of the next on phones), previous / next buttons that hide at the ends, and a dot per position. Touch users swipe; the track is keyboard scrollable.

Composed of: [IconButton](#iconbutton), [PageDots](#pagedots)

```tsx
<Carousel perView={3} label="Features">{items.map((x) => <FeatureCard {...x} />)}</Carousel>
```

Full page: src/components/media/carousel/docs.md

## ChatBubble

One chat message. Mine is an Aktivite-blue gradient with light text, theirs the card color with a line. A run of one sender's messages tightens the inner corners and only the last bubble keeps the small "tail" corner. Inside: the sender's name in group chats (one of the four HADİ colors per sender), a reply quote with an orange bar, the text (emoji-only messages grow and lose the bubble), time and delivery ticks (sending · sent · delivered · read · failed with Retry) and reaction chips. Drag a bubble sideways to reply: an arrow appears, and past the threshold it fires when you let go while the bubble springs back on the motion engine.

Composed of: [Button](#button), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [ReplyQuote](#replyquote)

```tsx
<ChatBubble mine text="See you at 7" time={m.at} status="read" position="last" reactions={m.reactions} onReact={toggle} onReply={() => reply(m)} />
```

Full page: src/components/social/chat-bubble/docs.md

## ChatComposer

The message field of a chat. On the start side an attach Menu whose + turns 45° while it is open; in the middle a growing Textarea (Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line) with an emoji button that opens a ReactionPicker grid (the emoji goes in at the caret). On the end side one round button morphs on the motion engine: a microphone in Heyecan orange while the field is empty, a send arrow in Aktivite blue once there is text. Recording replaces the field with a pulsing dot, a running timer and a live waveform; the round button sends it, the trash button or Esc drops it. A reply preview with an orange bar sits above.

Composed of: [Menu](#menu), [Textarea](#textarea), [ReactionPicker](#reactionpicker), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [StatusDot](#statusdot), [ReplyQuote](#replyquote)

```tsx
<ChatComposer onSend={(text) => send(text)} onVoice={sendVoice} attachments={[photo, file]} replyTo={$reply} />
```

Full page: src/components/composite/chat-composer/docs.md

## ChatThread

A conversation. Messages become ChatBubbles grouped into runs per sender (5 minutes apart at most), with sticky day separators ("Today", "Yesterday", a date). The TypingIndicator sits under the last message; the smile button of a bubble opens a ReactionPicker under it. Motion: your new message rises from the composer on a spring, theirs slides in from its side. While you are at the bottom it follows new messages; scrolled up, they wait behind a "↓ N new" button. Rows are keyed, so an edit, a status or a reaction updates one bubble.

Composed of: [ChatBubble](#chatbubble), [TypingIndicator](#typingindicator), [ReactionPicker](#reactionpicker), [Avatar](#avatar), [Button](#button), [Picture](#picture)

```tsx
<ChatThread messages={$messages} typing={$typing} group onReact={toggleReaction} onReply={(m) => $replyTo = m} />
```

Full page: src/components/composite/chat-thread/docs.md

## CheckMark

The yes / no / partly mark of comparison tables, plan features and check lists: ✓, ✕ or – together with the text a screen reader reads. The text is visually hidden unless `text` shows it; every glyph and text can be replaced.

```tsx
<CheckMark value={row.included} />
<CheckMark value="partial" text />
<CheckMark value={false} variant="soft" label={false} />
<CheckMark value labels={{ yes: "Included" }} icons={{ yes: heart }} m:color="primary" size="lg" />
<CheckMark value={$done} variant="soft" motion="flip" />          // ✕ turns into ✓ when $done changes
<CheckMark value={$ok} motion={(next, prev) => animate(next, { opacity: [0, 1], transform: ["translateY(6px)", "none"] }, { duration: 240 }).finished} />
```

Full page: src/components/feedback/check-mark/docs.md

## Checkbox

One checkbox with its label. The box is drawn (the tick strokes in, the fill grows from the centre, it shrinks a little when pressed) while the real `<input>` stays for the keyboard, forms and screen readers. Looks: `classic`, `soft`, `chip`, `card` and `toggle`, each in three sizes and with the corner shapes that suit it (`shapesFor`).

```tsx
<Checkbox bind:value={$agree} label="I have read the terms" />
<Checkbox value={true} indeterminate label="Some items selected" />
<Checkbox variant="card" label="Team plan" hint="Up to 10 people" icon={users} />
```

Full page: src/components/forms/checkbox/docs.md

## CheckboxGroup

Several checkboxes; the value is the array of checked option values. Every Checkbox look works (`chip` and `card` are the usual ones for groups), `inline` lays them in a row, and `colors="brand"` gives each option the next HADİ color.

```tsx
<Field label="Days" group><CheckboxGroup bind:value={$days} inline variant="chip" options={days} /></Field>
<CheckboxGroup variant="card" options={[{ value: "team", label: "Team", hint: "Up to 10 people", icon: users, meta: "$49" }]} />
```

Full page: src/components/forms/checkbox-group/docs.md

## Chevron

The small arrow that turns when something opens: an accordion header, a disclosure, a tree row, a grouped table row. It points to `direction` while closed and turns when open; right-to-left pages mirror it. Give it `open`, or leave it out and the arrow follows the nearest ancestor with `aria-expanded` (or the summary of an open `<details>`).

```tsx
<Chevron open={$open} />
<button aria-expanded={$open} onClick={toggle}>Details <Chevron direction="down" /></button>
<Chevron open={$open} direction="down" motion="spring" size="lg" m:color="primary" icon={arrowRight} />
<Chevron leaf />
```

Full page: src/components/actions/chevron/docs.md

## Chip

A label pill. Three uses: a static label, a **filter** you can switch on and off (`selected` + `onClick`, announced with `aria-pressed`), and a **removable** tag (`onRemove`, an ×-button with an accessible name).

Composed of: [OverflowText](#overflowtext), [IconButton](#iconbutton)

```tsx
<Chip>Design</Chip>
<Chip selected={$on} onClick={() => $on = !$on}>Open</Chip>
<Chip tone="primary" onRemove={() => remove(tag)}>{tag}</Chip>
<Chip icon={tag} selected={$on} selectedIcon={false} onClick={toggle}>Design</Chip>   // no tick: the icon stays
<Chip selected={$on} selectedIcon={heart} onClick={toggle}>Liked</Chip>              // your own mark
<Chip onRemove={drop} removeIcon={trash} removeLabel="Delete tag">{tag}</Chip>
```

Full page: src/components/actions/chip/docs.md

## ChoicePicker

One single-choice control that picks its look from the options, so option panels never show a drop-down for a handful of values. With `kind: "auto"`: 10 or more options → Combobox; options with a `preview` → preview cards; 2–6 short labels → Segmented; otherwise chips. Any other `kind` forces that look; `pickerKind(options)` tells which one auto picks.

Composed of: [Segmented](#segmented), [RadioGroup](#radiogroup), [Combobox](#combobox)

```tsx
<ChoicePicker bind:value={$align} options={["start", "center", "end"]} />           // segmented
<ChoicePicker bind:value={$blend} options={modes.map((m) => ({ value: m, label: m, preview: () => <Swatch mode={m} /> }))} kind="grid" />
```

Full page: src/components/forms/choice-picker/docs.md

## ClampText

Text folded to a number of lines, with a "more" switch that appears only when the text is really cut, and "less" to fold it again. Captions, bios, descriptions in cards and feeds.

Composed of: [Button](#button)

```tsx
<ClampText lines={3}>{post.text}</ClampText>
<ClampText text={bio} lines={2} open={$open} onOpenChange={(v) => $open = v} labels={{ more: "read on", less: "fold" }} />
<ClampText lines={2} expandable={false}>{title}</ClampText>
```

Full page: src/components/typography/clamp-text/docs.md

## CodeEditor

A small code field for one snippet: the text is coloured while it is typed (the CodeView colours; unfinished code too), a suggestion list opens at the caret, ranges can be marked (a flash for "this just changed", an underline for "this is wrong") and a foot line says what the owner thinks of the code. It does **not** run or compile anything: the owner reads `value` and decides what it means (the showcase reads a component's props from it).

Composed of: [EditorFrame](#editorframe), [Popover](#popover), [OptionList](#optionlist), [CopyButton](#copybutton), [Kbd](#kbd), [StatusDot](#statusdot)

```tsx
import { CodeEditor, jsxCompleter } from "hadi-march/ui";

<CodeEditor bind:value={$code} lang="tsx" message={$note} status={$bad ? "error" : "ok"}
  complete={jsxCompleter({ tag: "Button", props: [
    { name: "variant", hint: "look", values: ["primary", "secondary", "ghost"] },   // variant="…": values inside the quotes
    { name: "icon", hint: "icon", value: "={plus}" },                              // written as icon={plus}
    { name: "disabled" },                                                          // a bare prop
  ] })}
  marks={[{ from: 8, to: 23, kind: "flash" }]} />
<CodeEditor value={$css} onChange={save} lang="css" complete={(ctx) => ({ from: ctx.caret, items: [{ label: "color" }] })} />
<CodeEditor bind:value={$one} multiline={false} message={false} copy={false} />   // one bare line
```

Full page: src/components/composite/code-editor/docs.md

## CodeInput

One-time code and PIN boxes. Typing moves forward, Backspace back, ← → move, a paste fills from the box (extra characters are cut) and `onComplete` fires once when every box is filled. In the HADİ theme each box takes the next HADİ color and the display font, as in the HADİ apps; boxes shrink on narrow screens instead of overflowing.

```tsx
<CodeInput length={6} groups={[3, 3]} onComplete={verify} />
<CodeInput length={8} pattern="alphanumeric" colors="palette" font="mono" variant="filled" />
<CodeInput length={4} mask size="lg" />
```

Full page: src/components/forms/code-input/docs.md

## CodeView

A read-only code block: line numbers, syntax colours for js / ts / jsx / tsx, css, html, json and sh (other languages stay plain), a wrap toggle and a copy button. Text is inserted as text nodes, never as HTML. Every showcase Code tab draws it through the `code-view` widget point.

Composed of: [CopyButton](#copybutton), [Button](#button), [PanelHeader](#panelheader)

```tsx
<CodeView code={source} lang="tsx" copy />
<CodeView code={css} lang="css" lineNumbers={false} wrap />
```

Full page: src/components/typography/code-view/docs.md

## ColorInput

A color as `#rrggbb`: the native swatch picker and a text field side by side, kept in sync (typing a valid hex moves the swatch; picking a swatch writes the text).

Composed of: [Swatch](#swatch), [TextInput](#textinput)

```tsx
<Field label="Brand color"><ColorInput bind:value={$color} /></Field>
```

Full page: src/components/forms/color-input/docs.md

## ColorPicker

An advanced color picker: a saturation / brightness area, hue and alpha sliders, an eyedropper (where the browser has one), an old / new preview (click the old half to go back), the value as hex, rgb() or hsl() text (any CSS color can be typed or pasted), WCAG contrast on white and black, and palettes: the four HADİ colors, the theme's palette and the recent picks. Theme colors are read from the tokens at the moment they are picked, so they follow the active theme.

Composed of: [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Segmented](#segmented), [Badge](#badge), [SectionLabel](#sectionlabel), [Slider](#slider), [Swatch](#swatch), [TextInput](#textinput)

```tsx
<ColorPicker bind:value={$color} />
<ColorPicker value={brand} format="hsl" alpha={false} palettes={[{ label: "HADİ", colors: ["#0b5", "brand-blue"] }]} />
```

Full page: src/components/composite/color-picker/docs.md

## Combobox

A text field with a list of matching options: static `options` filtered as you type (accent and case-insensitive), or an async `search(q)` that is debounced, shows "Searching…" and ignores late answers. Arrow keys move, Enter picks, Escape closes. `multiple` turns it into chips (see MultiSelect); `allowCustom` lets typed text become the value.

Composed of: [Chip](#chip), [OptionList](#optionlist)

```tsx
<Field label="District"><Combobox bind:value={$town} options={towns} placeholder="Start typing" /></Field>
<Field label="Member"><Combobox bind:value={$userId} search={(q) => api.users(q)} labelOf={(id) => names[id]} /></Field>
```

Full page: src/components/forms/combobox/docs.md

## CommandPalette

Ctrl/⌘+K opens a search over every registered command, every NavMenu page and every action, ranked with typo tolerance. An optional `ask(query)` hook (an intent search the app provides) adds an "Ask" row: it runs on Enter, or by itself when local results are weak. Only a small shell ships with the page; the dialog loads on first open, and hovering or focusing a `PaletteButton` fetches it ahead of time.

Composed of: [Dialog](#dialog), [SearchBox](#searchbox), [ListRow](#listrow), [SectionLabel](#sectionlabel), [Empty](#empty), [Kbd](#kbd), [OverflowText](#overflowtext)

```tsx
<CommandPalette ask={(q) => api.intent(q)} placeholder="Search pages or actions…" />
<PaletteButton label="Search…" />
registerCommands([{ id: "doc.new", title: "New document", group: "Document", shortcut: "mod+alt+n", run: create }])
```

Full page: src/components/composite/command-palette/docs.md

## ConsentBanner

The consent manager's UI. A bottom banner asks until there is a valid decision for the current policy version (Reject all sits next to Accept all, with the same weight); the preferences panel lists every category as a Card with a Toggle (a Dialog on wide screens, a bottom sheet on phones); `ConsentGate` keeps third-party content behind a placeholder that can allow it in place. The module is lazy on purpose: load it with `lazy(() => import("hadi-march/managers/consent/ui"), { pick: "ConsentBanner" })`.

Composed of: [Button](#button), [Card](#card), [Dialog](#dialog), [Toggle](#toggle), [Stack](#stack), [Empty](#empty)

```tsx
<ConsentBanner title="Cookies" text="We use analytics to measure visits." />
<ConsentGate category="thirdParty">{() => <iframe src={videoUrl} title="Video" />}</ConsentGate>
```

Full page: src/components/composite/consent-banner/docs.md

## ContextMenu

The menu that opens where you right-click, or with Shift+F10 / the Menu key on the focused element. It draws the same items as `Menu` — plain items, actions, separators, shortcuts — with the same roving keyboard; `items` receives the element that was clicked, so one menu can offer different entries for different targets.

Composed of: [Menu](#menu)

```tsx
<ContextMenu items={(target) => [{ label: "Copy", shortcut: "mod+c", onSelect: copy }, "-", { label: "Delete", danger: true, onSelect: remove }]}>
  <ul class="files">…</ul>
</ContextMenu>
```

Full page: src/components/overlays/context-menu/docs.md

Copies text to the clipboard. The button says "Copied" (or swaps its icon for a tick) for a moment and announces it; when the clipboard is not available a toast reports the failure.

Composed of: [Button](#button), [IconButton](#iconbutton)

```tsx
<CopyButton text="npm i hadi-march" />
<CopyButton text={() => token} iconOnly label="Copy key" />
<CopyButton text={link} icon={share} label="Copy link" copiedLabel="Link copied" copiedIcon={heart} copiedColor="brand-blue" duration={3000} />
<CopyButton text={code} errorText={false} onError={report} />   // no toast: you handle the failure
```

## CornerMark

A small round mark in a corner of a picture, a card or an avatar: the video sign on a photo tile, the arrow that appears on a project cover, the "+" badge on a story ring. The parent must be positioned (`position: relative`).

```tsx
<div class="tile"><Picture source={photo} fit="cover" /><CornerMark icon={video} /></div>
<a class="card m-corner-host" href={href}>…<CornerMark icon={arrowUpRight} variant="surface" show="hover" /></a>
<CornerMark corner="bottom-end" icon={plus} variant="solid" m:color="brand-orange" size="sm" ring overlap />
```

Full page: src/components/media/corner-mark/docs.md

## CountRoll

An odometer number for likes, comments and followers. When the value changes only the digits that changed roll: upward when it grows, downward when it shrinks, on the motion engine (global speed, pause and reduced motion apply). The text is compact in the active locale (`1,2 B`, `12K`); `format="full"` groups it instead.

```tsx
<CountRoll value={$likes} />
<CountRoll value={$followers} format="full" />
```

Full page: src/components/social/count-roll/docs.md

## Counter

An animated number. It counts up when it scrolls into view and glides to every new value; `mode="roll"` turns each digit like an odometer (only the digits that change move). Formatting follows the locale through `Intl.NumberFormat`: grouping, decimals, currency, percent, compact.

Composed of: [CountRoll](#countroll)

```tsx
<Counter value={12840} />
<Counter value={$price} mode="roll" format={{ style: "currency", currency: "EUR" }} />
<Counter value={0.98} format={{ style: "percent" }} />
<Counter value={$n} mode="none" />                       // no motion: the value just changes
<Counter value={12840} duration={3000} easing="bounce" />
```

Full page: src/components/landing/counter/docs.md

## CtaBand

The "ready to start?" band near the end of a page: a rounded panel with a title, a lead and actions over a themed background — `gradient` (brand colours), `mesh`, `glass`, `plain` or `video`. A light follows the pointer; the panel scales in when it scrolls into view.

Composed of: [SiteSection](#sitesection), [Reveal](#reveal), [VideoBackground](#videobackground), [SectionHead](#sectionhead)

```tsx
<CtaBand variant="gradient" title="Start today" lead="…"
  actions={[{ label: "Try free", href: "/start", iconEnd: arrowRight }, { label: "Talk to sales" }]} note="14 days free" />
<CtaBand title="Start today" reveal="up" />                     // another entrance
<CtaBand title="Start today" backdrop={false} reveal="none" class="my-band" />   // a bare panel, no motion: style it yourself
```

Full page: src/components/landing/cta-band/docs.md

## DataGrid

A spreadsheet-like grid for large data. It runs on the table engine (`createTable`: sorting, filters, search, column layout, selection, inline edit, CSV) and the shared virtual window, which windows **rows and columns**: only the cells in view are in the DOM, so 100 000 rows × many columns scroll smoothly. On top it adds grouping with aggregates, a totals footer, pinned columns, drag to reorder and resize columns, and a keyboard cell cursor.

Composed of: [SearchBox](#searchbox), [Button](#button), [Chip](#chip), [Menu](#menu), [Checkbox](#checkbox), [Chevron](#chevron), [Badge](#badge), [ResizeHandle](#resizehandle), [Empty](#empty), [LiveStatus](#livestatus), FilterControl, CellEditor

```tsx
import { DataGrid } from "hadi-march/components/data/data-grid";

<DataGrid rows={$orders} rowKey="id" selectable groupBy={["region"]}
  columns={[
    { key: "customer", label: "Customer", pin: "left", editable: true },
    { key: "region", label: "Region", filter: "select" },
    { key: "amount", label: "Amount", format: ["money", "USD"], aggregate: "sum" },
  ]}
  onEdit={(row, key, value) => save(row.id, key, value)} />
```

Full page: src/components/data/data-grid/docs.md

## DatePicker

A date typed in the locale's own order (`14.03.2026`, `3/14/2026`) with a Calendar popover. The value is an ISO date string or `null`; an impossible date (`31.02`) or one outside `min` / `max` marks the field invalid instead of changing the value. `parseDate` and `formatDate` are the same rules as functions.

Composed of: [Calendar](#calendar), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Popover](#popover)

```tsx
<Field label="Date"><DatePicker bind:value={$date} min={todayIso()} /></Field>
parseDate("14.3.2026", "de") // "2026-03-14"
```

Full page: src/components/forms/date-picker/docs.md

## DateRangePicker

A date range `{ from, to }` (either end may be open). Presets — today, the last 7 / 30 / 90 days, this month — sit in a Segmented row; "Custom" shows a from / to pair of DatePickers that keep each other in order. `rangePresets(today)` returns the built-in presets for your own list.

Composed of: [Segmented](#segmented), [DatePicker](#datepicker)

```tsx
<Field label="Report period" group><DateRangePicker bind:value={$range} /></Field>
<DateRangePicker bind:value={$range} presets={false} max={todayIso()} />
```

Full page: src/components/forms/date-range-picker/docs.md

## DateTimeInput

A date and a time edited side by side, stored as one ISO timestamp in UTC (like `new Date().toISOString()`) and shown in local time. Picking only a date uses `defaultTime`.

Composed of: [DatePicker](#datepicker), [TimeInput](#timeinput)

```tsx
<Field label="Starts"><DateTimeInput bind:value={$startsAt} defaultTime="09:00" /></Field>
```

## DevicePreview

Shows content as on a real phone or tablet: the device body with its camera (island, punch hole or notch), the status bar (time, signal, battery), the home indicator, the real screen size in CSS pixels, portrait or landscape. The mouse acts like a finger: the cursor becomes a touch dot, dragging scrolls whatever is under it (with a fling that slows down), a long press opens the context menu, a drag never also clicks.

Composed of: [OverlayScope](#overlayscope)

```tsx
import { DevicePreview, DEVICES } from "hadi-march/layout";

<DevicePreview device="iphone-15"><MySite /></DevicePreview>
<DevicePreview device="ipad" landscape touch={false}>…</DevicePreview>
<DevicePreview device={{ name: "Kiosk", width: 1080, height: 1920, radius: 0, kind: "screen" }}>…</DevicePreview>
```

## Dialog

A modal window over the page. Declarative: `<Dialog open={…} onClose={…}>`; imperative: `openDialog(render)` and `openDrawer(render)` return a promise that resolves with the value passed to `close(value)`. `confirm`, `prompt` and `askReason` are ready-made dialogs; `closeAll()` and `openDialogs()` manage the stack.

Composed of: Portal, [PanelHeader](#panelheader), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Button](#button), Field, [TextInput](#textinput), [Textarea](#textarea), [Select](#select), [Drawer](#drawer)

```tsx
<Dialog open={$open} onClose={() => $open = false} title="Invite" footer={<Button variant="primary">Send</Button>}>…</Dialog>
```

Full page: src/components/overlays/dialog/docs.md

## Disclosure

A collapsible section built on the native `<details>` / `<summary>` elements, so keyboard and screen reader support come for free and the browser's find-in-page opens it. The summary line has a turning chevron and the body opens with an animation. `open` can be a signal; `onToggle` reports the new state.

Composed of: [Chevron](#chevron)

```tsx
<Disclosure title="Advanced settings" open={false} onToggle={(open) => save({ advanced: open })}>
  <AdvancedForm />
</Disclosure>
```

Full page: src/components/layout/disclosure/docs.md

## DockLayout

An IDE workspace, the dock of march-app-ui (after HADİ Studio Kit): tab groups in rows and columns. Drag a tab to a **side** of a group (a new split), onto its **centre** or **between two tabs** (a tab there), or to the **outer edge** of the whole layout. Closing never deletes: the group **collapses to a strip** (vertical in a row, horizontal in a column) and gets its size back when opened. Groups fill the whole area, layouts come from presets and are saved as plain JSON. Panels never move in the DOM: an iframe keeps running, an editor keeps its state.

Composed of: [Tabs](#tabs), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Button](#button), [ResizeHandle](#resizehandle), [Menu](#menu)

```tsx
<DockLayout panels={[
  { id: "files", title: "Files", icon: folder, min: [150, 120], content: () => <FileTree /> },
  { id: "editor", title: "main.ts", icon: fileText, content: () => <Editor />, dirty: () => $dirty },
  { id: "console", title: "Console", icon: terminal, content: () => <Console /> },
]} presets={{ main: { title: "Main", tree: () => row([.26, tabs("files")], [.74, col([.68, tabs("editor")], [.32, tabs("console")])]) } }}
   persist="ide.layout" api={(a) => dock = a} />
```

Full page: src/components/composite/dock-layout/docs.md

## Drawer

A sheet that slides in from an edge: `start` / `end` (mirrored in right-to-left layouts), `top` or `bottom`. It can be dragged toward its edge to close, rest on snap points, and be modal (scrim, focus trap, the page inert) or non-modal (the page stays usable).

Composed of: Portal, [Dialog](#dialog)

```tsx
<Drawer open={$open} onClose={() => $open = false} side="bottom" snapPoints={[0.4, 0.9]} title="Filters">…</Drawer>
```

Full page: src/components/overlays/drawer/docs.md

## EasingCurveEditor

Edit a `cubic-bezier()` easing by its two handles and watch it run. The preview runs on the motion engine's clock, so the global speed, "Stop all" and reduced motion apply to it; a faint dot moves linearly beside the eased one, and a marker rides the curve. The presets are the engine's named curves. With `name`, every change registers the curve in the engine (`defineEasing`), so any animation can use it by name.

Composed of: [Card](#card), [Button](#button), [NumberInput](#numberinput)

```tsx
<EasingCurveEditor bind:value={$easing} name="hadi-pop" />
animate(card, frames, { duration: 600, easing: "hadi-pop" })
```

Full page: src/components/motion/easing-curve-editor/docs.md

The frame of an editor: a border with a focus ring around a head bar (toolbar, search, tabs, status), the editing area and a foot bar (counts, hints). MarkdownEditor, RichTextEditor and TreeEditor are drawn in it; an editor of your own gets the same look.

```tsx
<EditorFrame head={<FormatToolbar onTool={exec} />} actions={<Badge>{$words} words</Badge>} foot={<span>Markdown</span>}>
  <textarea class="m-editor-area" bind:value={$text} />
</EditorFrame>
<EditorFrame showHead={() => $tools.length > 0} headProps={{ sticky: true }} footProps={{ divider: true }} color="brand-green" />
```

## Empty

What a list, table or page shows when it has nothing yet: an icon in a raised tile, a title, a line of text and the next step as buttons. An empty screen that says what to do next.

Composed of: [IconTile](#icontile)

```tsx
<Empty icon={inbox} title="No messages yet" action={[<Button variant="primary" icon={plus}>New message</Button>]}>Start a conversation or invite a teammate.</Empty>
```

An error shown in place of the content that failed: the message of an `Error` (or any value, as text), an optional title and a "Retry" button.

```tsx
<ErrorBox title="Could not load" error={err} retry={() => refetch()} />
```

## ExplodedView

Takes what it holds apart, like an exploded drawing, and puts it back. Nothing is drawn again: the **same** elements tilt and rise (their state, focus and listeners stay), so what comes apart is exactly what was on screen.

```tsx
import { ExplodedView } from "hadi-march/ui";

<ExplodedView bind:open={$apart} onPick={(id) => $picked = id} active={$picked}
  parts={[{ selector: ".m-avatar", label: "Avatar" }, { selector: ".m-like", label: "LikeButton", level: 2 }]}>
  <PostCard post={post} />
</ExplodedView>
<ExplodedView open={$apart}><Button icon={plus}>New project</Button></ExplodedView>     // the layers of the button
<ExplodedView open layers={{ ring: false, surface: "Background" }} gap={32} tilt={{ x: 46, z: -24 }} motion="spring" tags={false} fit={false} />
```

Full page: src/components/layout/exploded-view/docs.md

## Faq

Frequently asked questions as an Accordion. `split` puts the heading and a contact line at the start (sticky) and the questions at the end; `search` adds a SearchBox that narrows the list with the shared fuzzy ranking (accent- and case-insensitive, typo tolerant) and announces how many questions match.

Composed of: [Accordion](#accordion), [SearchBox](#searchbox), [Empty](#empty), [SectionHead](#sectionhead)

```tsx
<Faq layout="split" search title="Questions" lead="…" contact={<Button variant="secondary">Write to us</Button>}
  items={[{ q: "Is it free?", a: "Yes, MIT licensed." }, …]} />
<Faq search items={…} count={false} reveal="none"
  labels={{ search: "Type a word", empty: "Nothing found. Write to us.", count: (shown, total) => `${shown} / ${total}` }} />
```

## FeatureGrid

What a product does, as a grid: `cards` (Cards with an IconTile; a soft light follows the pointer across the grid), `plain` (no boxes), `list` (icon beside the text, two columns) or `bento` (tiles of different sizes with optional media). Items enter one after another; tiles in a row share one height; on phones everything stacks.

Composed of: [Grid](#grid), [Card](#card), [ListRow](#listrow), [IconTile](#icontile), [Reveal](#reveal)

```tsx
<FeatureGrid variant="bento" items={[
  { icon: zap, title: "Fast", body: "…", span: "big", media: <Screenshot /> },
  { icon: shieldCheck, title: "Secure", body: "…" },
  { icon: globe, title: "Every language", body: "…", span: "wide" },
]} />
<FeatureGrid variant="cards" cols={3} items={features} />
<FeatureGrid items={features} spotlight={false} reveal="none" />     // no pointer light, no entrance
<FeatureGrid items={features} reveal={{ from: { opacity: 0, transform: "rotate(-4deg) scale(.9)" }, to: { opacity: 1, transform: "rotate(0deg) scale(1)" } }} />
```

## Feed

A social feed. PostCards sit in a VirtualList, so only the posts near the viewport are in the DOM, inside a PullToRefresh (the feed is the scroll area; keyboard users get a Refresh button). The first page shows skeleton posts; reaching the end loads the next page with a skeleton at the bottom (infinite scroll) and an end mark once there is nothing more. New posts waiting above show a "N new posts" pill that merges them and scrolls to the top.

Composed of: [PullToRefresh](#pulltorefresh), [VirtualList](#virtuallist), [PostCard](#postcard), [Skeleton](#skeleton), [Button](#button), [Empty](#empty), [StatusDot](#statusdot)

```tsx
<Feed posts={$posts} hasMore={$more} onRefresh={reload} onLoadMore={next} onLike={like} onOpenMedia={open} />
```

Full page: src/components/composite/feed/docs.md

## FileUpload

Drop files or click to choose. `accept` and `maxSize` are checked before anything is kept (the reasons are listed); images and audio get a preview (object URLs are revoked on cleanup). With an `upload(file, { onProgress, signal })` function each file shows its progress and can be cancelled, and the value becomes what `upload` resolves with.

Composed of: [Progress](#progress), [ListRow](#listrow), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Button](#button), [Badge](#badge)

```tsx
<FileUpload multiple accept="image/*" maxSize={5_000_000} label="Drop images or choose" />
<FileUpload bind:value={$urls} multiple upload={(file, { onProgress, signal }) => api.upload(file, onProgress, signal)} />
```

## FlowCanvas

A node editor on an endless canvas: pan and zoom, snap to the grid, nodes with ports and form fields, bezier edges, values flowing along the edges as moving dots, box and multi selection, copy / paste, undo, a minimap, layered auto layout, groups, a context menu and full keyboard use. The flow lives in a store (`createFlow`) that FlowPalette adds to and FlowControls runs; it reads and writes a readable JSON schema (`march.flow/v1`).

Composed of: [ContextMenu](#contextmenu), [IconButton](#iconbutton), Toolbar, [OverflowText](#overflowtext), [IconTile](#icontile), [StatusDot](#statusdot), [CheckMark](#checkmark), [Alert](#alert), Field, [TextInput](#textinput), [NumberInput](#numberinput), [Select](#select), [Toggle](#toggle), [Button](#button), [CopyButton](#copybutton), [UndoRedo](#undoredo), [JsonEditor](#jsoneditor), [FlowControls](#flowcontrols), [FlowPalette](#flowpalette), [Tabs](#tabs)

```tsx
const flow = createFlow({ types, doc })          // types: [{ type, label, icon, color, inputs, outputs, fields, run }]
<FlowCanvas flow={flow} snap={16} minimap />
flow.toJSON()                                     // { schema: "march.flow/v1", nodes, edges: [{ from: "hook.out", to: "check.in" }], groups }
flow.load(JSON.parse(text), "Import")             // validated (validateFlow); one undo step
```

Full page: src/components/composite/flow-canvas/docs.md

## FlowControls

Run, pause, step and reset a flow; choose the speed; see the state, the clock and how many nodes finished. `createFlowRunner(flow)` executes the flow node by node and writes the state FlowCanvas draws: the running node glows, a failing node shakes and shows its error, values travel along the edges as dots and every edge counts what passed. `FlowTimeline` is the run record: one bar per executed node on a time axis with a playhead.

Composed of: [Button](#button), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Segmented](#segmented), [Chip](#chip), [Card](#card), [TimeRuler](#timeruler), [ListRow](#listrow), [Badge](#badge), [Empty](#empty)

```tsx
const runner = createFlowRunner(flow, { nodeMs: 650, travelMs: 560 })
<FlowControls runner={runner} flow={flow} timeline />
await runner.run()        // "done" | "error"; runner.pause() / resume() / step() / reset()
```

Full page: src/components/composite/flow-controls/docs.md

## FlowPalette

The node types of a flow, grouped by category, with a search box (accent and Turkish-letter insensitive). Drag a card onto a FlowCanvas to place the node where you drop it, snapped to the grid; a click or Enter adds it in the middle of the view. The dragged card floats in the drag layer, tilts while it is held and melts into the canvas (or flies back when dropped outside) on the motion engine.

Composed of: [SearchBox](#searchbox), [OverflowText](#overflowtext), [ListRow](#listrow), [IconTile](#icontile), [SectionLabel](#sectionlabel), [Empty](#empty)

```tsx
const flow = createFlow({ types })
<FlowPalette flow={flow} />
<FlowCanvas flow={flow} />
```

Follow, Following or Requested (a private account asks first), with a morph between them: the pill's width springs from one label to the other, the filled Aktivite background turns into an outline, the + turns into a tick, and a small burst of the four HADİ colors marks a new follow (motion engine; with reduced motion only the state changes). Hovering "Following" turns it red before you unfollow.

```tsx
<FollowButton state={$state} name={user.name} onChange={(s) => $state = s} />
```

## FontPicker

Choose a typeface. The fonts of the device and a web font catalog (Google Fonts by default: about 1,900 open-licensed families) sit in one searchable list. Each name is drawn in its own type, a specimen shows your own sample text with size, weight and italic, and the list narrows by category, subset, order and favourites. It opens as a popover by its button, as a dialog, or sits inline in a settings page. The value is the family name; `onPick` hands over the CSS to use it.

Composed of: [Popover](#popover), [Dialog](#dialog), [SearchBox](#searchbox), [Segmented](#segmented), [Select](#select), [VirtualList](#virtuallist), [ListRow](#listrow), [SectionLabel](#sectionlabel), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Button](#button), [Textarea](#textarea), [Slider](#slider), [Toggle](#toggle), [CopyButton](#copybutton), [Alert](#alert), [Empty](#empty)

```tsx
<FontPicker bind:value={$font} onPick={(f) => setStyle(page, { "font-family": f.stack, "font-weight": f.weight })} />
<FontPicker view="dialog" askConsent preview="sample" sample="Hello world" bind:value={$font} />
<FontPicker view="inline" source="/fonts" category="serif" favorites={false} bind:value={$font} />
<FontPicker catalog={ownFamilies} source={(r) => `/fonts/${r.family}.css`} system={false} bind:value={$font} />
```

The formatting bar of a text editor: bold, italic, headings, lists, link, undo and redo. MarkdownEditor and RichTextEditor use it; put it over your own editor and apply the format in `onTool`.

## Gantt

A project timeline. Each task is a bar on a day / week / month scale with its progress filled in; dependency arrows link a predecessor's end to its successor's start (red and dashed while they overlap). Drag a bar to move it, drag its ends to resize it, drag the knob under it to set progress. With `cascade`, successors that would start before their predecessor ends are pushed later, keeping their length. A today line marks the current day; the task names stay pinned while the timeline scrolls.

Composed of: [ListRow](#listrow), [ResizeHandle](#resizehandle), [Badge](#badge), [LiveStatus](#livestatus)

```tsx
import { Gantt } from "hadi-march/components/data/gantt";

<Gantt tasks={$tasks} scale="day" cascade
  onChange={(task) => api.save(task)}
  onSelect={(task) => open(task)} />
```

Full page: src/components/data/gantt/docs.md

## GradientEditor

Build a CSS gradient by hand. Pick the type (linear, radial, conic), turn the angle dial or press a quick angle, click the stop bar to add a color stop (its color is the gradient's color at that point), drag stops to move them, drag one down (or press Delete) to remove it, and edit the selected stop's color with a full ColorPicker. Presets start from the HADİ colors and the theme palette; the CSS is ready to copy.

Composed of: [ColorPicker](#colorpicker), [Card](#card), [Stack](#stack), [Segmented](#segmented), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Swatch](#swatch), [NumberInput](#numberinput), [CopyButton](#copybutton)

```tsx
<GradientEditor bind:value={$background} />
<GradientEditor value="radial-gradient(circle, #ffd27a 0%, #f2801f 100%)" types={["radial"]} presets={false} />
```

Full page: src/components/composite/gradient-editor/docs.md

## Grid

A responsive grid that never overflows horizontally. Fixed columns (`cols`, 1–6) step down on tablets and phones, or `min` gives automatic columns of at least that width. The last row can share the remaining space (`fill="stretch"`) or give it to the last item (`fill="last"`), and `balance` picks the column count that spreads items evenly over the rows (5 in 4 columns → 3 + 2, not 4 + 1). `equal` makes every row as tall as the tallest. Pure CSS (grid, flex-wrap and `:has()`); no measuring script.

```tsx
<Grid cols={4} gap={3} fill="stretch" balance>{cards}</Grid>
<Grid min="16rem">{cards}</Grid>
```

Full page: src/components/layout/grid/docs.md

## Hero

The first screen of a website in seven looks that share one structure: an eyebrow pill, a large title whose `highlight` gets the brand gradient, a lead, actions and a note. The stage changes by variant: `centered` (soft grid and spotlight), `split` (media at the end), `video` (VideoBackground), `mesh` (gradient mesh, spotlight, grain), `aurora` (drifting colour), `product` (a product frame that tilts in 3D and flattens as you scroll) and `parallax` (layered depth).

Composed of: [Reveal](#reveal), [Overlay](#overlay), [Badge](#badge), [VideoBackground](#videobackground), [Parallax](#parallax), [Picture](#picture), [SectionHead](#sectionhead)

```tsx
<Hero variant="mesh" eyebrow="New: 2.0" title="The fastest way to build a website" highlight="fastest"
  lead="…" note="No card needed" actions={[{ label: "Start free", href: "/start", iconEnd: arrowRight }, { label: "Watch demo" }]} />
<Hero variant="product" media={{ src: "/screen.png", alt: "Dashboard", width: 1600, height: 1000 }} … />
<Hero variant="video" video={{ src: "/clip.webm", poster: "/clip.jpg" }} … />
<Hero variant="mesh" title="…" backdrop={false} reveal="none" />              // no decorative layers, no entrance
<Hero variant="product" title="…" media={…} frameBar={false} tilt={false} reveal="blur" />
<Hero eyebrow="New" eyebrowHref="/news" eyebrowArrow={<Icon of={arrowRight} />} title="…"
  reveal={{ from: { opacity: 0, transform: "scale(.9)" }, to: { opacity: 1, transform: "scale(1)" } }} />
```

## HonestCompare

A comparison table that also shows where the product is behind. A cell is `true` (yes), `false` (no), `"partial"` or any text / node (not scored). In every scored row the `us` column is compared with the best other column: ahead, even or behind. Behind rows get a mark and keep their `note` visible (why, what is planned). The summary counts the rows, and a toggle shows only the rows where the product loses.

Composed of: [Badge](#badge), [Button](#button), [CheckMark](#checkmark)

```tsx
<HonestCompare
  columns={[{ id: "us", name: "HADİ" }, { id: "events", name: "Event sites" }]}
  rows={[
    { label: "Nearby events by time", values: { us: true, events: "partial" } },
    { label: "Ticketing", values: { us: false, events: true }, note: "Not planned: HADİ is for free meetups." },
    { label: "Price", values: { us: "Free", events: "Fee per ticket" } },
  ]} />
<HonestCompare columns={…} rows={…} m:color="brand-green" tags={false} filter={false}
  labels={{ partly: "Half", behind: "We lose", counts: (c) => `${c.ahead} wins, ${c.behind} losses` }}
  renderCell={(value, { us }) => (value === true && us ? "✓✓" : undefined)} />   // undefined keeps the default mark
```

Full page: src/components/landing/honest-compare/docs.md

## HorizontalScroll

A pinned section whose panels move sideways while the page scrolls down: the vertical distance equals the track's overflow, so the last panel arrives as the section ends. A progress line follows. RTL moves the other way. On touch screens and with reduced motion it is a native horizontal scroller with snap points.

Composed of: [Progress](#progress)

```tsx
<HorizontalScroll label="Case studies" panel="26rem">
  {cases.map((c) => <Card>…</Card>)}
</HorizontalScroll>
<HorizontalScroll progress={false}>…</HorizontalScroll>   // no progress line
<HorizontalScroll pinned={false}>…</HorizontalScroll>     // never pins: a sideways scroller with snap points
```

Full page: src/components/landing/horizontal-scroll/docs.md

## IconButton

A button that shows only an icon. `label` is required: it becomes the accessible name (`aria-label`) and the native tooltip (`title`), so an icon-only control is never unnamed. Leaving it out throws while you develop.

```tsx
<IconButton icon={heart} label="Like" on:click={like} />
<IconButton icon={trash} label="Delete" variant="danger" size="sm" />
<IconButton icon={star} label="Star" m:color="brand-gold" title={false} />   // coloured, no native tooltip
<IconButton icon={pin} label="Pin" size="xs" pressed={$pinned} on:click={toggle} />        // toggle: aria-pressed + pressed look
<IconButton icon={send} label="Send" variant="solid" shape="round" m:color="brand-blue" />   // filled circle
<IconButton icon={arrowUp} label="Back to top" variant="raised" shape="round" />           // floating button
<IconButton icon={x} label="Close" inverse />                                              // on a photo / video
<IconButton icon={globe} label="Website" href="https://example.com" />                     // a link
```

Full page: src/components/actions/icon-button/docs.md

An icon in a tinted, rounded square: the lead of a card, a list row, an empty state or a flow node. The tint is one of nine named tones or any theme colour token.

```tsx
<IconTile icon={users} tone="primary" />
```

## ImageCropper

Crop an image the way phones do: the frame stays centered, the picture moves under it. Drag the image to move it, zoom with the wheel, the slider or + −, turn it by 90° with the buttons (or R) and by fine angles with the angle slider (or [ ]), mirror it (F), resize the frame from its corners or pick an aspect ratio. At any angle the image always covers the frame, so the result never has empty corners. The result is drawn on a canvas (`api.toCanvas()`, `api.toBlob()`); a small live preview shows it with its size in pixels.

Composed of: [Card](#card), [Segmented](#segmented), [Slider](#slider), [IconButton](#iconbutton)

```tsx
<ImageCropper src={url} bind:value={$crop} aspect={1} api={(c) => cropper = c} />
const blob = await cropper.toBlob("image/webp", 0.9, 512)
```

## JsonEditor

JSON in two views. **Text**: the source with live parse errors (line and column), Format and Tab indentation. **Tree**: a TreeEditor with type badges, inline editing and undo, loaded the first time the view is opened (a form that only needs the text view stays small). A `schema` (JSON Schema subset) and `validate` check both views: the text view lists the first problem with its path, the tree marks every invalid row.

Composed of: [TreeEditor](#treeeditor), [Textarea](#textarea), [Button](#button), [Tabs](#tabs)

```tsx
<JsonEditor bind:value={$settings} mode="tree" schema={schema} />
<JsonEditor bind:value={$raw} modes={["text"]} validate={(v) => (v.version ? null : "version is required")} />
```

Full page: src/components/composite/json-editor/docs.md

## KeyframeTimeline

Edit and play a keyframe animation on the motion engine. Each track animates one property (x, y, scale, rotate, opacity) of a target; its lane shows the value curve and the keyframes as diamonds you drag along time (snapped, Alt for free). Scrub the ruler or drag the playhead; play, pause, loop and change the speed. The selected keyframe has its time, value and an EasingCurveEditor for the curve into it. Playback is a motion engine `Playback`, so the global speed, "Stop all" and reduced motion apply; `timelineCode(model)` writes the same animation as engine timeline code.

Composed of: [EasingCurveEditor](#easingcurveeditor), [Card](#card), [TimeRuler](#timeruler), [ListRow](#listrow), [StatusDot](#statusdot), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Segmented](#segmented), [NumberInput](#numberinput)

```tsx
<KeyframeTimeline bind:value={$scene} />
<KeyframeTimeline value={model} snap={100} loop={false} renderTarget={(name) => <img src={`/${name}.svg`} alt="" />} />
```

```tsx
const DocsLayout = Layout.extend({ aside: <Toc/>, features: { readingProgress: true } })

const help = defineLayoutFeature("help", () => (api) => api.add("bottom-start", <HelpButton/>))
<Layout features={{ help: true }}>…</Layout>

<Page title="Kullanıcılar" layout={{ aside: <Filters/> }} corners={{ "bottom-end": <NewUser/> }}>…</Page>
```

## LiveCounter

A number that grows while you watch. Feed it a live value (a signal from your server), or give it a start and a `rate` per minute: it then adds small random steps on the motion clock, only while it is on screen. Every part is yours: how the digits change, the live dot, the "+N" bubble that rises on every increase, and the small beat of the number.

Composed of: [Counter](#counter), [Badge](#badge), [StatusDot](#statusdot)

```tsx
import { splitFlap } from "hadi-march/motion/text"
<LiveCounter value={$online} label="people online" />
<LiveCounter from={18420} rate={40} effect={splitFlap} effectOptions={{ duration: 900 }} dotColor="brand-orange"
  bubble={(diff) => <b>❤ {diff}</b>} beat={false} label="joined an event this week" />
<LiveCounter value={$n} effect="none" dot={false} bubble={false} />
```

Full page: src/components/landing/live-counter/docs.md

## LiveFeed

A living wall: new activity slides in at the top (rows) or pops into the first cell (wall), and the oldest leaves, so the page looks inhabited. Feed it a reactive list (`items`, newest first: from a socket or a store) or a `next()` function the feed calls every `every` ms while it is on screen. It starts full and keeps its size: a leaving item is lifted out of the flow while it fades and wall cards share one height, so the page never shifts.

Composed of: [Avatar](#avatar), [Button](#button), [ListRow](#listrow), [StatusDot](#statusdot)

```tsx
<LiveFeed next={() => nextActivity()} every={2400} max={5} />
<LiveFeed items={$events} variant="wall" live="polite" />
<LiveFeed next={next} enter="drop" leave="fall" glow={false} />
<LiveFeed next={next} enter={{ keyframes: { opacity: [0, 1], transform: ["rotate(-6deg) scale(.8)", "none"] }, duration: 500 }} />
<LiveFeed next={next} pauseLabel="On air · stop" resumeLabel="Stopped · go on" pulse={false} pauseOnHover={false}
  renderItem={(item) => <><b>{item.title}</b> <small>{item.meta}</small></>} />   // own rows, own button texts
<LiveFeed next={next} enter="none" leave="none" glow={false} move={false} />        // no motion at all
```

Full page: src/components/landing/live-feed/docs.md

## LiveStatus

The line that says what just changed: "3 selected", "21–40 of 120", "Build: 9 – 13 Nov". It is a polite live region, so screen readers hear the change without focus moving. Shown as text where the number is useful to everyone (a table footer), or only read (`visible={false}`) where sighted users already see the change (a dragged event). With `help` a hint line comes before it; give it `helpId` and point the widget at it with `aria-describedby`.

```tsx
<LiveStatus text={() => `${$count} selected`} />
<LiveStatus visible={false} text={$moved} help="Drag an event to move it" helpId="plan-help" />
<section aria-describedby="plan-help">…</section>
```

Full page: src/components/feedback/live-status/docs.md

## Loader

A loading state that fills an area: a large spinner with a line of text under it (or only for screen readers). Inline it takes the place of the content; with `overlay` it covers its positioned container with a translucent scrim. `bootLoader.done()` fades out the static `#m-boot` screen of `index.html` once the app has rendered.

Composed of: [Spinner](#spinner)

```tsx
<Loader text="Preparing dashboards…" />
```

Full page: src/components/feedback/loader/docs.md

## LogoCloud

"Trusted by" logos. `grid` lines them up in equal cells that light up on hover; `marquee` runs them as an endless ticker (Marquee: edges fade, it stops off screen, reduced motion keeps it still). Logos share one muted tone by default and show their colour on hover.

Composed of: Marquee, [Grid](#grid), [Picture](#picture), [Reveal](#reveal)

```tsx
<LogoCloud title="Trusted by teams at" variant="marquee" logos={[
  { name: "HADİ", src: "/logos/hadi.svg", width: 120, height: 32 },
  { name: "Northwind", node: <NorthwindLogo /> },
]} />
<LogoCloud logos={logos} reveal="up" />     // grid: another entrance; reveal="none": the logos are simply there
```

An optional credit line: "Developed with March and 💗", with "March" as a link. Using it is a request, not a requirement: the licence stays MIT and nothing here is needed to use March.

```tsx
<MadeWithMarch />
<MadeWithMarch variant="badge" />
<MadeWithMarch variant="small" />
<MadeWithMarch heart="☕" heartLabel="Coffee" />              // your own mark
<MadeWithMarch heart={false} />                              // "Developed with March"
<MadeWithMarch text={(link, heart) => <>Built on {link} {heart}</>} link="March UI" />
```

## MarkdownEditor

Markdown source with a live preview. Four views: **write**, **preview**, **split** (resizable; both panes scroll together) and **rich** (the same value in a RichTextEditor, loaded the first time it is opened). The toolbar and shortcuts write Markdown syntax as native undo steps (Ctrl+Z keeps working); Enter continues lists and quotes, Tab / Shift+Tab indent list lines; HTML pasted from a web page or an office suite becomes Markdown through the safe content core.

Composed of: [EditorFrame](#editorframe), [FormatToolbar](#formattoolbar), [Splitter](#splitter), [Tabs](#tabs), [RichTextEditor](#richtexteditor)

```tsx
<MarkdownEditor bind:value={$doc} view="split" />
<MarkdownEditor value={md} views={["write", "preview"]} toolbar={false} />
<MarkdownEditor bind:value={$doc} view="rich" stats={false} />
```

## Media

One element for images, video and audio: it fits its container, guesses the kind from the extension (`kind="auto"`), shows controls for video and audio, and swaps in a text fallback when the file fails to load. `openMedia(url)` shows it in a dialog.

Composed of: [Dialog](#dialog)

```tsx
<Media src={url} kind="auto" alt="Hills at dusk" poster={thumb} />
```

Full page: src/components/media/media/docs.md

## MediaGrid

The photos of a post in one frame: one photo keeps its own shape (between 4:5 and 1.91:1), two sit side by side, three are one large and two stacked, four are a 2×2 grid, and more show "+N" on the last tile. Each tile is a button that opens the photo; a Skeleton shimmers until the image arrives and it then fades in. With `onDoubleTap` a single tap waits 230 ms, so a double tap (like) never also opens the photo.

Composed of: [Skeleton](#skeleton), [CornerMark](#cornermark), [Picture](#picture)

```tsx
<MediaGrid items={post.media} onOpen={(i, el) => openLightbox(post.media, i, el)} onDoubleTap={() => like(post)} />
```

Full page: src/components/social/media-grid/docs.md

## Menu

A trigger button with a floating menu. Items are plain entries (`label`, `icon`, `onSelect`, `href`, `shortcut`, `danger`, `disabled`, `hidden`, `can`, `checked`, `radio`), `action()` objects (their guard, confirmation and toasts come along) or separators (`"-"`). `args` are passed to every action and `onSelect`.

Composed of: [Button](#button), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Popover](#popover), [ListRow](#listrow), [CheckMark](#checkmark), [Kbd](#kbd), Divider

```tsx
<Menu label="Actions" icon={more} items={[{ label: "Edit", icon: edit, shortcut: "E", onSelect: edit }, "-", remove]} args={[row]} />
<Dropdown label="Filters">{(close) => <FilterForm onDone={close} />}</Dropdown>
```

Full page: src/components/actions/menu/docs.md

## MultiSelect

Several values as chips in one field. It is a Combobox with `multiple`: the same static options or async search, the same keyboard; Backspace in the empty field removes the last chip and each chip has its own remove button.

Composed of: [Combobox](#combobox)

```tsx
<Field label="Languages"><MultiSelect bind:value={$langs} options={[{ value: "tr", label: "Turkish" }, { value: "en", label: "English" }]} /></Field>
```

## NavMenu

Sidebar navigation for big apps. Items are grouped (collapsible groups with icons), can be pinned, and the recently used ones are listed first; a filter box narrows the list with accent- and case-insensitive search. The active item follows the router path, and the pages are registered with the command palette. On narrow screens the menu becomes a drawer opened by a menu button; `collapsible` adds an icon rail on wide screens. UI state persists in localStorage. NavSidebar is the richer sidebar built on the same container.

Composed of: [ListRow](#listrow), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [SearchBox](#searchbox), [Badge](#badge), [Chevron](#chevron), [SectionLabel](#sectionlabel), [Empty](#empty), [Drawer](#drawer)

```tsx
<NavMenu brand={<Brand />} items={[
  { id: "inbox", title: "Inbox", href: "/inbox", icon: inbox, badge: () => $unread },
  { id: "users", title: "Users", href: "/users", icon: users, group: "Admin" },
]} />
```

## NavSidebar

The app's side menu: categories that open and close, a typo-tolerant search over every item, recent visits and featured items at the top, a collapsible icon rail and a resizable width, all remembered per user. Items are links (router `Link`), so the current page is marked and the menu follows navigation.

Composed of: [ListRow](#listrow), [SearchBox](#searchbox), [PanelHeader](#panelheader), [SectionLabel](#sectionlabel), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Button](#button), [Badge](#badge), [Chevron](#chevron), [Empty](#empty), [ResizeHandle](#resizehandle), [Drawer](#drawer)

```tsx
<NavSidebar title="HADİ" items={[
  { id: "/orders", label: "Orders", href: "/orders", group: "Sales", icon: cart, badge: () => $open },
  { id: "/users", label: "Users", href: "/users", group: "Admin", can: "users.read" },
]} collapsible resizable groupOrder={["Sales", "Admin"]} />
```

## Newsletter

An email sign-up, inline (field and button on one line) or stacked. While sending, the button shows its spinner; on success the form folds away and a check with the thank-you line pops in; on an error the field shakes and the message is announced.

Composed of: [TextInput](#textinput), [Button](#button), [CheckMark](#checkmark), [SectionHead](#sectionhead)

```tsx
<Newsletter title="Stay in the loop" lead="One email a month."
  onSubmit={(email) => api.subscribe(email)} note="Unsubscribe any time." />
<Newsletter onSubmit={save} button="Join" done="You are in." doneIcon={<Icon of={heart} />} motion={false}
  labels={{ email: "Your email", invalid: "That does not look like an email.", error: "Could not save. Try again." }} />
```
