## NotForYou

The anti-landing block: it says plainly who the product is **not** for, and optionally who it is for. With `check`, every "not for you" line is a toggle card: red at first, with "That's me" and a small "Not you? Tap it!"; a tap strikes the line out, turns the card green and reveals the item's positive side (`instead`), with `markedHint` under the label ("You belong here"). A verdict under the list says how many still apply.

Composed of: [CheckMark](#checkmark), [ListRow](#listrow)

```tsx
<NotForYou check items={[{ text: "You run a 1,000-seat conference", detail: "No ticketing; an event platform fits better." }]}
  forYou={[{ text: "You want to do something tonight" }]} />
<NotForYou variant="list" items={…} verdict={(n, total) => `${n}/${total}`} />
<NotForYou check items={…} meLabel="Sounds like me" hint="Tap if not" markedHint="Welcome"
  mark={(state) => (state === "not" ? "🙅" : state === "marked" ? "🎉" : "👍")} />   // own marks and texts
<NotForYou check items={…} mark={false} meLabel={false} hint={false} markedHint={false} verdict={false} title={false} />
```

Full page: src/components/landing/not-for-you/docs.md

## NumberInput

A locale-aware number: accepts `12,5` and `12.5`, never produces `NaN` (bad text marks the field invalid and is put back on blur), clamps to `min` / `max` and steps with ArrowUp / ArrowDown. The family: **IntInput** (0 decimals), **MoneyInput** (the currency symbol on the locale's side, the currency's decimals, grouping) and **PercentInput** (shows 12.5 % for a stored 0.125).

```tsx
<Field label="Quantity"><NumberInput bind:value={$n} min={0} max={99} /></Field>
<Field label="Price"><MoneyInput bind:value={$price} currency="EUR" /></Field>
<Field label="Discount"><PercentInput bind:value={$rate} /></Field>
```

Full page: src/components/forms/number-input/docs.md

## OptionList

A list of choices inside a panel: a theme or accent picker, a type menu, the suggestions under a field. Each row has a lead (icon, swatch, avatar), a label, a hint, a trailing part and a tick when chosen. It is a radio group by default, a listbox (one or many) or a menu of commands; a field can drive it with its own keys (`keysFrom`).

Composed of: [ListRow](#listrow), [SectionLabel](#sectionlabel)

```tsx
<OptionList bind:value={$theme} label="Theme"
  options={[{ value: "light", label: "Light", icon: sun }, { value: "dark", label: "Dark", icon: moon, hint: "Easy on the eyes" }]} />
<OptionList multiple bind:value={$columns} options={columns} label="Columns" />
<OptionList mode="menu" options={blockTypes} onPick={(type) => insert(type)} />             // commands
<SearchBox inputRef={(el) => input = el} debounce={0} bind:value={$q} />
<OptionList keysFrom={() => input} options={$matches} onPick={choose} empty="No match" />    // suggestions
```

Full page: src/components/forms/option-list/docs.md

## OverflowText

Text that scrolls only when it does not fit; text that fits stays put. It starts on hover or focus of its nearest link, button or list item (or always, or while visible), and moves in one of three modes: bounce to the end and back, an endless loop with a separator, or once. The clipped edges fade on the logical side (RTL scrolls the other way), screen readers read the text once, and under reduced motion it does not move: the end fades and the full text is in the tooltip. `Marquee` is the endless ticker preset (`trigger="visible"`, `mode="loop"`).

```tsx
<OverflowText text={title} />
<Marquee text="New: dark theme · faster search · RTL" separator="✦" />
```

Full page: src/components/typography/overflow-text/docs.md

## OverflowToolbar

A toolbar that never wraps or squeezes: items that do not fit move to a **More** menu, lowest `priority` first, and come back (with a short slide-in) when there is room again. An item is a plain action or a **command id**: the Command manager then supplies its label, icon, shortcut, availability and busy state, so the palette, menus and this toolbar always agree.

Composed of: [Button](#button), [IconButton](#iconbutton), Divider, [Menu](#menu), [Tooltip](#tooltip)

```tsx
<OverflowToolbar label="Document" items={[
  { id: "new", label: "New", icon: plus, onSelect: create, priority: 10 },
  { id: "save", command: "doc.save", priority: 9 },
  { id: "s1", separator: true },
  { id: "split", label: "Split", icon: columns, pressed: () => $split, onSelect: () => $split = !$split },
  { id: "delete", label: "Delete", icon: trash, danger: true },
]} />
<OverflowToolbar label="Document" items={items} moreLabel="Other tools" moreIcon={menu} tooltips={false}
  motion="fade" m:color="brand-purple" />
<OverflowToolbar label="Document" items={items} motion={(el) => animate(el, { opacity: [0, 1], y: [-8, 0] }, { duration: 240 })} />
```

Full page: src/components/actions/overflow-toolbar/docs.md

## Overlay

A decorative layer that lives inside its container: an image, a muted looping video that plays only while visible, an inline SVG, a canvas drawn by a function every frame, or a CSS effect (`glass`, `gradient`, `mesh`, `noise`, `vignette`, `spotlight`, `grid`, `dots`). Layers stack in the order they are added; `front` puts one above the content. They never take pointer input.

```tsx
<section class="hero"><Overlay src="media/waves.webm" poster="media/waves.jpg" /><Overlay effect="vignette" /><h1>Title</h1></section>
```

Full page: src/components/media/overlay/docs.md

## OverlayScope

A box that layers opened inside it open in. A drawer, a dialog, a menu or a toast of a site preview, a device frame, a dashboard panel or a component demo stays in it instead of covering the whole page.

```tsx
import { OverlayScope } from "hadi-march/layout";

<OverlayScope class="preview"><MySite /></OverlayScope>      // its SiteNav drawer opens inside the preview

openDrawer(render)                         // inside a scope: in the scope (found from the component or the focus)
openDrawer(render, { target: "page" })     // the whole page anyway
<Portal layer="popover" target={el}>…</Portal>
```

Full page: src/components/layout/overlay-scope/docs.md

## PageDots

One dot per page; the current one is longer and takes the accent colour. Under a carousel, beside a story, in an onboarding flow. With `onChange` (or `bind:value`) the dots are buttons; without it they only show where you are.

```tsx
<PageDots count={5} bind:value={$page} />
<PageDots count={steps.length} value={$active} m:color="brand-orange" />
<PageDots count={4} value={$i} onChange={(i) => $i = i} dot={(i) => i + 1} />
```

Full page: src/components/navigation/page-dots/docs.md

## Pagination

Numbered pages with ellipses: the first and last pages, the current page and `siblings` pages on each side stay visible, the rest collapse into a gap. Previous / Next buttons are disabled at the ends. Pages are 1-based. `variant="simple"` draws only Previous / Next, with a page count or without one (cursor mode).

Composed of: [Button](#button), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Select](#select)

```tsx
<Pagination bind:page={$page} pages={20} />
```

Full page: src/components/navigation/pagination/docs.md

## PanelHeader

The bar on top of a panel: a dialog, a drawer, a window, a dock group, a card, a board column, an editor. A lead slot, an icon, the title and a second line, free content, a count, the actions and the close button. Every part is optional and yours to replace. `as="footer"` draws the same bar under a panel (status text + actions).

Composed of: [IconButton](#iconbutton)

```tsx
<PanelHeader icon={settings} title="Settings" subtitle="Workspace" divider
  actions={<Button size="sm">Save</Button>} onClose={() => $open = false} />
<PanelHeader size="sm" tone="muted" title="index.ts" actions={<CopyButton text={code} />} />      // editor / code bar
<PanelHeader title="To do" meta={<Badge>{$cards.length}</Badge>} lead={<StatusDot />} />           // board column
<PanelHeader as="footer" title="3 changes" actions={<Button size="sm">Apply</Button>} divider />   // bottom bar
<PanelHeader drag title={$title} titleAs="span" titleId={id} ref={(bar) => track(bar, move)}
  role="toolbar" tabindex="0" onKeyDown={onKey} onDblClick={toggleMax} onClose={close} />          // window title bar
```

Full page: src/components/layout/panel-header/docs.md

## Parallax

Layered depth. Each layer (an image or any node, placed with Overlay) moves at its own speed while the section scrolls past and, with `pointer`, shifts with the mouse by its depth, smoothed on the motion engine clock. Transform only; layers get room to travel so no edge shows.

Composed of: [Overlay](#overlay)

```tsx
<Parallax pointer={1} layers={[
  { src: "/sky.jpg", speed: 0.5 },
  { src: "/hills.png", speed: 0.25 },
  { content: <Shapes />, speed: -0.15 },
]}>
  <h2>Depth</h2>
</Parallax>
```

Full page: src/components/landing/parallax/docs.md

A password field with a Show / Hide button. `autocomplete` defaults to `current-password`; use `new-password` on sign-up forms so password managers offer to generate one.

```tsx
<Field label="Password" help="At least 10 characters"><PasswordInput bind:value={$pw} autocomplete="new-password" /></Field>
```

## PeriodNav

Previous · today · next: the small group a calendar steps its period with. Without a title the three buttons are one joined control (the Scheduler bar); with a `title` the period's name sits between the arrows (the month row of a Calendar) and the today button follows. The arrows swap in right-to-left text.

Composed of: [ButtonGroup](#buttongroup), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Button](#button)

```tsx
<PeriodNav onPrev={() => shift(-1)} onNext={() => shift(1)} onToday={() => go(today)} />
<PeriodNav title={$monthName} onPrev={back} onNext={on} />
<PeriodNav title={$monthName} onPrev={back} onNext={on} onToday={now} today="This month" m:color="brand-orange"
  prevIcon={arrowLeft} nextIcon={arrowRight} labels={{ group: "Month", previous: "Previous month", next: "Next month" }} />
```

## PhoneInput

A phone number stored as `+` and digits (`"+447700900123"`). With `country` the calling code is shown as a prefix and put in front of national numbers; `normalizePhone(text, country)` is the same rule as a function.

```tsx
<Field label="Phone"><PhoneInput bind:value={$phone} country="+44" /></Field>
normalizePhone("0 (532) 111-22-33", "+90") // "+905321112233"
```

## Picture

The image element behind every "cover", "logo" or "media" slot. Such a slot takes a picture object (`{ src, alt, width, height, srcset, sizes }`) or a ready node; Picture draws the object as an `<img>` (lazy, decoded off the main thread, with its size so nothing jumps) and returns a node as it is. `isPicture(x)` tells the two apart.

```tsx
<Picture source={project.cover} fit="cover" />
<Picture src="/hero.jpg" alt="Hills at dusk" width={1200} height={800} loading="eager" />
<Picture source={<MyChart />} />
```

Full page: src/components/media/picture/docs.md

## Popover

A trigger and a floating panel next to it: filters, a column picker, a link form, a date panel, a list of choices. The panel is placed beside the trigger (and flips at the screen edge), closes on a press outside or Escape, takes focus when it opens and gives it back to the trigger. The open state is its own or yours.

Composed of: [PanelHeader](#panelheader), [Button](#button)

```tsx
<Popover trigger={<Button icon={filter}>Filters</Button>} title="Filters" placement="bottom-end"
  footer={<Button size="sm" variant="primary" onClick={apply}>Apply</Button>}>
  {(close) => <FilterForm onDone={close} />}
</Popover>
<Popover trigger="Sort" flush>{(close) => <OptionList bind:value={$sort} options={sorts} onPick={() => close()} />}</Popover>
<Popover bind:open={$open} anchor={() => input} role="listbox" flush autoFocus={false} motion="none">
  <OptionList keysFrom={() => input} options={$suggestions} onPick={insert} />
</Popover>
```

One post of a social feed. The header shows the author (Avatar, name with a verified mark), the relative time and the place, with an optional ⋯ Menu. Photos sit in a MediaGrid; a double tap on them likes the post with a large heart that pops over the photo and bursts in the four HADİ colors. The action row has a LikeButton and rolling counts for comments and shares; the caption folds to three lines with a "more" button.

Composed of: [Card](#card), [Avatar](#avatar), [Menu](#menu), [MediaGrid](#mediagrid), [LikeButton](#likebutton), [CountRoll](#countroll), [Button](#button), [ClampText](#clamptext), [ListRow](#listrow), [VerifiedMark](#verifiedmark)

```tsx
<PostCard post={post} onLike={(on) => like(post, on)} onComment={openComments} onOpenMedia={(i, el) => openLightbox(post.media, i, el)} />
```

## Presentation

Slides in the browser. `<Presentation>` holds `<Slide>`s; `<Appear>` reveals its children one per step. Arrow keys, Page Up / Down, Space, Home / End, the wheel (full screen), swipes and the buttons move through it; `F` goes full screen and `P` opens the speaker window. Slides change with a slide, fade or zoom transition (mirrored in RTL). The slide number can live in the URL. The speaker view shows the current and next slide, the notes and a timer, and every window of the same deck stays in step. Printing (or saving as PDF) puts each slide on its own page with all steps visible.

Composed of: [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Pagination](#pagination), [Progress](#progress), Toolbar

```tsx
let $slide = Number(queryParam("slide")() ?? 0)
<Presentation bind:index={$slide} transition="slide" presenterUrl="#/talk?presenter=1">
  <Slide layout="title" tone="brand" notes="Welcome everyone">…</Slide>
  <Slide notes="Three points, one by one"><h2>Why?</h2><Appear><li>Fast</li><li>Accessible</li><li>Beautiful</li></Appear></Slide>
</Presentation>
```

Full page: src/components/landing/presentation/docs.md

## Pricing

Plans side by side with a monthly / yearly switch. Switching morphs every price: the digits roll to the new amount (Counter, odometer mode), the "billed" line cross-fades and the switch thumb slides. The featured plan is lifted with a brand-gradient border. Cards share one height; on phones they stack with the featured plan first.

Composed of: [Card](#card), [Badge](#badge), [Segmented](#segmented), [Counter](#counter), [CheckMark](#checkmark), [Reveal](#reveal)

```tsx
let $period = "monthly"
<Pricing bind:period={$period} saving="2 months free" currency="EUR" plans={[
  { name: "Starter", price: 0, features: ["1 project", "Community support"], cta: { label: "Start free" } },
  { name: "Pro", price: { monthly: 29, yearly: 24 }, featured: true, badge: "Most popular", features: […], cta: { label: "Go Pro" } },
  { name: "Enterprise", price: null, features: […], cta: { label: "Talk to sales" } },
]} />
```

## ProfileHeader

The top of a profile. A cover (a photo, or a soft art of the four HADİ colors) with a bottom dim; the avatar in a StoryRing that overlaps it and opens the stories; the name with a verified mark, the handle and the bio; stats as buttons with rolling counts; a FollowButton, a Message button and a ⋯ Menu. Following adds you to the followers, so the count rolls together with the button's morph. On your own profile an Edit button replaces follow and message.

Composed of: [Card](#card), [StoryRing](#storyring), [FollowButton](#followbutton), [CountRoll](#countroll), [Button](#button), [Menu](#menu), [Picture](#picture), [StatTile](#stattile), [VerifiedMark](#verifiedmark)

```tsx
<ProfileHeader user={u} follow={$f} onFollow={(s) => $f = s} onMessage={openChat} onStat={openList} />
```

## Progress

A progress bar with a label and the percentage, or an indeterminate one while the amount is unknown. Tones for meaning, three sizes, and several colours laid out as a gradient, equal segments or a flowing cycle (HADİ: the four brand colours by default).

```tsx
<Progress value={$p} label="Uploading" showValue />
```

Full page: src/components/feedback/progress/docs.md

## ProjectDetail

The page of one project: a back button, a big title, the facts (role, client, year, services as chips), the cover — marked as the shared element, so a ProjectGrid card can grow into it — the story, a gallery that opens in the Lightbox and the next project.

Composed of: [Button](#button), [KeyValue](#keyvalue), [Chip](#chip), openMedia, [Reveal](#reveal), [Picture](#picture), [SectionHead](#sectionhead)

```tsx
let $open: Project | null = null
const open = (p, cover) => sharedTransition(`project-${p.id}`, cover, () => { $open = p })
<If when={$open}>{(p) => <ProjectDetail project={p} onBack={() => $open = null} next={{ project: nextOf(p), onOpen: open }} />}
<Else><ProjectGrid projects={work} onOpen={open} /></Else></If>
```

Full page: src/components/landing/project-detail/docs.md

## ProjectGrid

Portfolio work as cover cards with filter chips. Choosing a filter fades out what no longer matches and glides the rest into their new places (FLIP); new matches scale in. Opening a card hands its cover to `onOpen` — for a shared element transition into ProjectDetail — or, without it, shows the cover in the Lightbox.

Composed of: [Card](#card), [Chip](#chip), openMedia, [CornerMark](#cornermark), [Picture](#picture), [Reveal](#reveal)

```tsx
<ProjectGrid projects={work} onOpen={(p, cover) => sharedTransition(`project-${p.id}`, cover, () => { $open = p })} />
<ProjectGrid projects={work} />
```

Full page: src/components/landing/project-grid/docs.md

## PropertyGrid

An inspector: property rows in collapsible groups, a search field, and for each property the form control of its type. Every change is an **undo step** in the app's Undo history (typing in one field merges into one step), unsaved changes are registered with **DirtyState** (leave warning, `saveAll()`), and changed rows are marked and can be reset one by one. The footer counts the changes and offers Revert and Save.

Composed of: [Disclosure](#disclosure), [SearchBox](#searchbox), [PanelHeader](#panelheader), [UndoRedo](#undoredo), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Button](#button), [Badge](#badge), [StatusDot](#statusdot), [SectionLabel](#sectionlabel), [Empty](#empty), [TextInput](#textinput), [NumberInput](#numberinput), [Slider](#slider), [Toggle](#toggle), [Select](#select), [Segmented](#segmented), [ColorInput](#colorinput), [Textarea](#textarea)

```tsx
<PropertyGrid label="Card" bind:value={$card} onSave={(v) => api.save(v)} properties={[
  { key: "title", label: "Title", group: "Content" },
  { key: "width", label: "Width", type: "number", unit: "px", group: "Layout", validate: (v) => v > 420 ? "At most 420" : null },
  { key: "elevated", label: "Shadow", type: "switch", group: "Look" },
  { key: "radius", label: "Radius", type: "slider", min: 0, max: 24, group: "Look", hidden: (v) => !v.elevated },
]} />
```

Full page: src/components/composite/property-grid/docs.md

## PullToRefresh

A scroll area that refreshes when its top is pulled down past a threshold, by touch, pen or mouse. A spinning indicator follows the pull and keeps turning until the async `onRefresh` settles.

Composed of: [Button](#button)

```tsx
<PullToRefresh onRefresh={() => api.get("/feed").then((x) => $items = x)}>…</PullToRefresh>
```

## RadioGroup

Radio buttons; the value is the chosen option value. Same looks as CheckboxGroup plus `segmented` (joined buttons). Radio boxes are always round.

```tsx
<Field label="Size" group><RadioGroup bind:value={$size} inline options={["S", "M", "L", "XL"]} /></Field>
<RadioGroup variant="card" bind:value={$plan} options={plans} />
```

Full page: src/components/forms/radio-group/docs.md

## Rating

Stars to give or show a score. Editable it is a radio group: click or use the arrow keys (mirrored in right-to-left layouts), Home / End; hovering previews the score in a lighter tone. Read-only it can show half stars (`4.5`).

```tsx
<Rating bind:value={$stars} />
```

Full page: src/components/forms/rating/docs.md

## ReactionPicker

A row of emoji to react with, or a grid that serves as an emoji panel. It pops in (a spring scale and staggered emoji on the motion engine); the picked emoji sits on a soft Aktivite circle; hovering lifts an emoji. Arrow keys move between emoji (mirrored in RTL; up / down move by rows in the grid), Home / End jump.

Composed of: [IconButton](#iconbutton)

```tsx
<ReactionPicker selected={msg.myReaction} onPick={(e) => react(msg, e)} />
<ReactionPicker layout="grid" onPick={insertAtCaret} />
```

Full page: src/components/social/reaction-picker/docs.md

## ReplyQuote

The small box that shows which message is being answered: who said it and a cut of what was said, behind a coloured bar. ChatBubble draws it over an answer; ChatComposer draws it above the field as the "replying to" preview.

Composed of: [ClampText](#clamptext), [IconButton](#iconbutton)

```tsx
<ReplyQuote name="Deniz Kaya" text={m.text} />
<ReplyQuote variant="inverse" name="Deniz Kaya" text={m.text} onClick={() => jumpTo(m)} />
<ReplyQuote name="Replying to Deniz" text={m.text} lines={1} onClose={() => $replyTo = null} />
```

Full page: src/components/social/reply-quote/docs.md

## ResizeHandle

The ready element of the resize-handle behavior: a thin strip on an edge (or a corner) of what it resizes, with one look everywhere — a line that lights up on hover, focus and while dragging. With `value` + `set` it is a complete separator (drag, arrow keys, Home / End, Enter or double click resets, ARIA). Without them it is the bare grip for an owner that runs its own gesture (a window corner, the end of a calendar event).

```tsx
<aside class="panel">                                       {/* the parent is positioned */}
  …
  <ResizeHandle value={() => $w} set={(w, done) => { $w = w; if (done) save(w) }} min={160} max={480}
    reset={() => $w = 240} label="Sidebar width" />
</aside>
<th>Name <ResizeHandle value={() => width(col)} set={(w) => setWidth(col, w)} min={60} tabindex="-1" /></th>
<ResizeHandle edge="top" value={() => $h} set={(h) => $h = h} grip />                    // a bottom panel
<ResizeHandle edge="between" value={() => $ratio} set={setRatio} scale={() => 100 / width} line="always" />
<ResizeHandle edge="bottom-end" onPointerDown={startResize} onStep={(dx, dy) => resizeBy(dx, dy)} />   // a corner
```

Full page: src/components/layout/resize-handle/docs.md

## Reveal

Children enter when the block scrolls into view: fade, rise, fall, slide from the start or the end (mirrored in RTL), scale, blur or a 3D flip, one after another. `scrub` ties the effect to the scroll position. The motion engine plays it (transform, opacity, filter); with reduced motion the content is simply there.

```tsx
<Reveal effect="up" stagger={80}>
  <Card>…</Card><Card>…</Card><Card>…</Card>
</Reveal>
<ul use:revealOnScroll={{ effect: "start" }}>…</ul>
<Reveal effect="blur" scrub>…</Reveal>
```

Full page: src/components/landing/reveal/docs.md

## RichTextEditor

A rich text field whose value is **Markdown**. Write with the toolbar, keyboard shortcuts or Markdown shortcuts (`# `, `## `, `- `, `1. `, `> `, ```` ``` ````); mention people with `@`, insert emoji with `:`; pasted HTML from any site or office suite is cleaned through the safe content core (allowlist, no HTML parser — Trusted Types safe). Undo / redo use an UndoManager history of the editor's own (typing merges into one step).

Composed of: [EditorFrame](#editorframe), [FormatToolbar](#formattoolbar), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Avatar](#avatar), [Popover](#popover), [OptionList](#optionlist), Field, [TextInput](#textinput)

```tsx
<RichTextEditor bind:value={$notes} mentions={team} placeholder="Write…" />
<RichTextEditor value={md} toolbar={["bold", "italic", "link", "|", "ul", "ol"]} emoji={false} />
<RichTextEditor api={(e) => editor = e} />   // editor.insert("**Hi**"), editor.exec("h2"), editor.undo()
```

Full page: src/components/composite/rich-text-editor/docs.md

## Roadmap

A Timeline whose line fills as you scroll: a product roadmap, a company story or a work history. Every entry has a status (`done`, `now`, `next`); the dot of each entry the fill has passed lights up and the current one glows. The fill is a transform written in the scroll scene's write phase.

Composed of: [Timeline](#timeline), [Badge](#badge), [Progress](#progress), [Reveal](#reveal)

```tsx
<Roadmap items={[
  { time: "2025 Q1", title: "First release", body: "…", status: "done" },
  { time: "2026 Q3", title: "Teams", body: "…", status: "now" },
  { time: "2027", title: "Plugins", body: "…", status: "next" },
]} />
```

Full page: src/components/landing/roadmap/docs.md

## RowTools

The tools at the end of a row in an editable list: move up, move down, remove. Give it the row's `index` and the list's `count` and the arrows switch off on the first and the last row.

Composed of: [IconButton](#iconbutton)

```tsx
<RowTools index={i} count={() => rows().length} onUp={() => move(i, -1)} onDown={() => move(i, 1)} onRemove={() => remove(i)} />
<RowTools actions={["remove"]} onRemove={() => remove(i)} danger />
```

Full page: src/components/forms/row-tools/docs.md

## Scheduler

A month / week / day calendar of events. Drag an event to move it (minutes snap to `step`; across columns it changes day), drag its edge to resize it, drag on an empty slot to create one. Dates and times are formatted with Intl in the current locale: month and weekday names, the first day of the week, 12 / 24 hour clock and the reading direction. Overlapping events share the column width; all-day and multi-day events sit in their own lane as bars.

Composed of: [PanelHeader](#panelheader), [PeriodNav](#periodnav), [Button](#button), [Segmented](#segmented), [ResizeHandle](#resizehandle), [LiveStatus](#livestatus)

```tsx
import { Scheduler } from "hadi-march/components/data/scheduler";

<Scheduler events={$events} view="week" step={15}
  onChange={(event, range) => api.update(event.id, range)}
  onCreate={(range) => $events = [...$events, { id: uid(), title: "New", ...range }]}
  onSelect={(event) => open(event)} />
```

Full page: src/components/data/scheduler/docs.md

## ScrollProgress

A thin bar that fills as the page (or one article) is read. Fixed to the top or inline; brand gradient or the accent. The fill is a transform written in the scroll scene's write phase; in RTL it fills from the right.

Composed of: [Progress](#progress)

```tsx
<ScrollProgress />
<ScrollProgress target={() => article} position="inline" paint="accent" />
```

Full page: src/components/landing/scroll-progress/docs.md

## ScrollStory

Scrollytelling. The media column stays pinned while the text steps scroll past; the step nearest the middle of the viewport is active — its picture cross-fades in, the dots follow, and with `theme` the section takes that step's colour. On phones the pinned media sits at the top and the steps flow under it.

Composed of: [PageDots](#pagedots)

```tsx
<ScrollStory steps={[
  { title: "Design", body: "…", media: <Mock />, color: "brand-orange" },
  { title: "Build", body: "…", media: <Chart />, color: "brand-blue" },
]} />
```

Full page: src/components/landing/scroll-story/docs.md

## ScrollToTop

A "back to top" button that appears once the page is scrolled down and scrolls back to the top smoothly (at once with reduced motion; it keeps its aim while content above loads). It follows whatever scrolls: the window or a scrolling container. By default it puts itself into the bottom-end page corner; in a Layout it is the `scrollToTop` feature (on by default).

Composed of: [IconButton](#iconbutton), [BottomRightControls](#bottomrightcontrols)

```tsx
import { ScrollToTop } from "hadi-march/ui";

<ScrollToTop />                          // once; shows after 320 px
<ScrollToTop threshold={600} order={-1} />
<ScrollToTop inline target={box} />      // in place, for a scrolling box
<ScrollToTop icon={chevronUp} m:color="brand-blue" motion="fade" label="Up" class="my-top" />
<ScrollToTop motion={(el, shown) => animate(el, { opacity: shown ? [0, 1] : [1, 0], rotate: shown ? [-90, 0] : [0, 90] }, { duration: 300, fill: "forwards" })} />
<ScrollToTop motion="none" smooth={false} />   // no animation at all
```

Full page: src/components/actions/scroll-to-top/docs.md

## SearchBox

The search field: an icon, the input, a clear button and a shortcut hint. The value is debounced (`debounce={0}` writes every keystroke at once), Escape clears, Enter searches now. With `controls` it is the input of a combobox that drives a list of options. Every part can be turned off or replaced.

Composed of: [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Kbd](#kbd)

```tsx
<SearchBox bind:value={$q} onSearch={(q) => load(q)} shortcut />                      // "/" focuses it
<SearchBox size="sm" debounce={0} bind:value={$filter} placeholder="Filter…" />        // a side panel filter
<SearchBox variant="plain" debounce={0} bind:value={$q} controls={listId}
  activeDescendant={() => `${listId}-${$active}`} onKeyDown={keys} shortcutHint="escape" />   // a palette input
<SearchBox icon={false} clear={false} inputRef={(el) => input = el} />
```

Full page: src/components/forms/search-box/docs.md

## SectionHead

The heading group of a page section: a small eyebrow, the title, a lead paragraph, the actions and a note, stacked and aligned as one block. Every part is optional; the title level, the scale and the alignment are yours, and the block can enter with Reveal when it scrolls into view.

Composed of: [Button](#button), [Reveal](#reveal)

```tsx
<SectionHead eyebrow="Features" title="Everything you need" lead="Components, theme, motion and speed in one kit." />
<SectionHead size="lg" title="Ready to build?" lead="Start in a minute."
  actions={[{ label: "Start free", href: "/start" }, { label: "Read the docs", href: "/docs" }]} note="No card needed" />
<SectionHead as="h1" size="xl" align="start" eyebrow={<Badge tone="primary">New</Badge>} eyebrowHref="/news"
  title={<>Build <em>faster</em></>} reveal />
<SectionHead as="h3" size="sm" align="start" title="Newsletter" lead="One mail a month." />
```

Full page: src/components/landing/section-head/docs.md

## SectionLabel

The small heading of a group inside a panel: a menu, a palette, a sidebar, a property grid, an editor side panel. Small, uppercase and faint, with an optional icon, a count and an actions slot at the end.

```tsx
<SectionLabel>Recent</SectionLabel>
<SectionLabel icon={star} count={$favorites.length}
  actions={<IconButton size="sm" icon={plus} label="Add" onClick={add} />}>Favorites</SectionLabel>
<SectionLabel as="h3" upper={false} rule>Typography</SectionLabel>
<SectionLabel as="li" role="presentation">Commands</SectionLabel>      // a group heading inside a listbox
```

## Segmented

A compact single choice: joined buttons, the chosen one raised. Use it for 2–6 short options (view modes, units, periods). Arrow keys move and select; only the chosen button is in the Tab order.

```tsx
<Segmented bind:value={$view} options={[{ value: "list", label: "List" }, { value: "grid", label: "Grid" }]} aria-label="View" />
```

Full page: src/components/forms/segmented/docs.md

## Select

The native `<select>`, so phones show their own picker. Option values keep their type: a number stays a number, an object stays the same object. For a handful of values prefer ChoicePicker or Segmented; for many, Combobox.

```tsx
<Field label="City"><Select bind:value={$city} options={cities} placeholder="Choose…" /></Field>
```

## SiteFooter

The end of a website: brand and a short line about the product, link columns, social links, an optional Newsletter and a bottom row (copyright, legal links, back to top). Columns fold to two per row on tablets and stack on phones; an optional big wordmark fills the last line.

Composed of: Brand, [Newsletter](#newsletter), [IconButton](#iconbutton)

```tsx
<SiteFooter brand={{ name: "HADİ", mark: logo }} about="…" wordmark="HADİ"
  columns={[{ title: "Product", links: [{ label: "Pricing", href: "/pricing" }] }]}
  social={[{ label: "Blog", href: "/blog", icon: globe }]}
  newsletter={{ title: "Newsletter", onSubmit: (e) => api.subscribe(e) }}
  legal={[{ label: "Privacy", href: "/privacy" }]} />
```

## SiteNav

The top bar of a website. Sticky; `transparent` starts see-through over a hero and turns to glass after a few pixels of scroll; `floating` is a centred glass pill; `shrink` lowers it once scrolled; `hide` slides it away while scrolling down and back when scrolling up. A pill slides under the hovered link (mirrored in RTL) and rests on the current one. Below 860 px the links move into a Drawer.

Composed of: Brand, [IconButton](#iconbutton), openDrawer

```tsx
<SiteNav mode="transparent" brand={{ name: "HADİ", mark: logo, href: "/" }}
  links={[{ label: "Features", href: "#features" }, { label: "Pricing", href: "#pricing", active: () => $section === "pricing" }]}
  actions={<><Button variant="ghost">Sign in</Button><Button>Start</Button></>} />
```

Full page: src/components/landing/site-nav/docs.md

## SiteSection

The frame of every website block: content width, vertical rhythm, a tone (plain, muted, inverse, brand) and an optional heading group (eyebrow, title, lead) that enters with Reveal. Pages are a stack of sections.

Composed of: [SectionHead](#sectionhead)

```tsx
<SiteSection eyebrow="Features" title="Everything you need" lead="…" tone="muted">
  <FeatureGrid items={features} />
</SiteSection>
```

Grey (or brand-tinted) shapes standing in for content that is loading: a few text lines or a block of a set height. Drawn in the shape of what comes, the page does not jump when the data arrives.

```tsx
{() => (loading() ? <Skeleton lines={3} /> : <Profile user={user()} />)}
```

A range slider with the value shown next to it (an `<output>`). `format` turns the number into text (a unit, a percentage, a label).

```tsx
<Field label="Volume"><Slider bind:value={$vol} min={0} max={100} format={(v) => `${v} %`} /></Field>
```

## Spacer

A flexible gap in a row: everything after it moves to the end of the row (the logical end, so it mirrors in RTL). The usual way to put a title on one side of a top bar and its actions on the other.

```tsx
<Stack direction="row" align="center"><Brand /><Spacer /><UserMenu /></Stack>
```

## Spinner

A ring that turns while something loads. Three sizes; in a multicolour theme (HADİ) it carries the brand colours, `colors` picks them (a list of colour tokens) or keeps it to one.

```tsx
<Spinner size="lg" colors="brand" label="Loading users" />
```

## Splitter

Two panes side by side with a handle between them. Drag the handle, or focus it and use ← → (mirrored in RTL), Home / End for the limits and Enter to go back to the initial share. Each pane keeps at least `min` of the width.

Composed of: [ResizeHandle](#resizehandle)

```tsx
<Splitter start={<FileList />} end={<Preview />} initial={0.35} min={0.2} label="Resize the file list" />
```

Full page: src/components/layout/splitter/docs.md

## Stack

Layout primitives. `Stack` lays children out in a column or a row with a gap from the spacing tokens (0–8), alignment and justification, and optional wrapping. `Toolbar` is a labelled bar of controls with an end slot. `Divider` is a horizontal rule, a labelled one ("or"), or a vertical separator between inline items.

```tsx
<Stack direction="row" gap={2} align="center" justify="between" wrap>…</Stack>
<Toolbar label="Filters" end={<Button>Export</Button>}>…</Toolbar>
<Divider label="or" />
```

Full page: src/components/layout/stack/docs.md

## StatTile

One value with its label: the numbers of a profile, an item of a stats band, a figure above a list. The value is text or a node (a Counter that rolls), a hint line is optional, and the tile becomes a button with `onClick` or a link with `href`. For a KPI box with a delta and a sparkline use the `StatTile` of `hadi-march/charts`.

```tsx
<StatTile value="128" label="Posts" />
<StatTile value={<Counter value={$followers} mode="roll" />} label="Followers" variant="tile" onClick={openFollowers} />
<StatTile value="$4,250" label="This month" hint="12% more than last month" align="start" size="lg" m:color="success" />
<dl><StatTile term value="42" label="Events" /></dl>
```

A row of big numbers that count up when the band scrolls into view (Counter), each with a label and an optional note. Plain, divided by lines, or as cards.

Composed of: [Counter](#counter), [Reveal](#reveal), [StatTile](#stattile)

```tsx
<StatsBand items={[
  { value: 12000, label: "teams", format: { notation: "compact" }, suffix: "+" },
  { value: 99.98, decimals: 2, suffix: "%", label: "uptime" },
```

## StatusBar

The strip at the bottom of an editor or app. Items sit at the **start** or the **end** (writing direction), are plain text or buttons (an action or a **command id** from the Command manager), and carry a tone: info, success, warn, danger, or busy (a breathing dot on the motion engine). When the bar is too narrow, the lowest `priority` items move to a "…" menu. Items marked `live` are announced when their text changes ("Saving…", "Saved").

Composed of: [ListRow](#listrow), [Menu](#menu), [Tooltip](#tooltip), [StatusDot](#statusdot)

```tsx
<StatusBar items={[
  { id: "branch", icon: gitBranch, text: "main", onSelect: pickBranch, priority: 5 },
  { id: "pos", side: "end", text: () => "Ln " + $line, priority: 4 },
  { id: "save", side: "end", text: () => $state, tone: () => $busy ? "busy" : "success", live: true, priority: 9 },
  { id: "format", side: "end", command: "editor.format" },
]} />
```

Full page: src/components/layout/status-bar/docs.md

## StatusDot

A small dot that shows a state: live, busy, changed, online. It takes a tone or a theme colour, can pulse, and is either an image with a name (`label`) or decoration next to text that already says it.

```tsx
<StatusDot tone="success" pulse label="Live" />
<StatusDot m:color="brand-orange" size="xs" />
<span><StatusDot tone="warn" pulse="blink" /> Unsaved</span>
```

Full page: src/components/feedback/status-dot/docs.md

## Stepper

Progress through stages, with motion that shows where you are going. Stepper draws Steps and adds a liquid highlight that stretches from the old step to the new one and settles there, and step panels that morph into each other: the old panel blurs and slides toward the past, the new one arrives from the future (mirrored in RTL) while the frame's height follows. Back / Next buttons and a step counter come with it.

Composed of: [Steps](#steps), [Button](#button)

```tsx
<Stepper steps={[{ title: "Cart" }, { title: "Address" }, { title: "Payment" }]} current={$step} onSelect={(i) => $step = i}
  panels={[<Cart />, <Address />, <Payment />]} onFinish={submit} />
```

Full page: src/components/navigation/stepper/docs.md

## Steps

Progress through stages. Done steps show a check, the current step is highlighted and marked for screen readers, the rest are upcoming. With `onSelect` every step is a button (a checkout that lets you go back); `vertical` stacks them with their descriptions. Stepper and Wizard are built on it.

Composed of: [CheckMark](#checkmark)

```tsx
<Steps steps={[{ title: "Account" }, { title: "Profile" }, { title: "Done" }]} current={$step} onSelect={(i) => $step = i} />
```

Full page: src/components/navigation/steps/docs.md

## StoryProgress

The segmented bars on top of a story. Segments before the current one are full, later ones empty, and the current one fills over its duration on the motion engine. The fill is an essential animation: it keeps time with reduced motion (the story would otherwise skip at once), while "pause all" and the global speed still apply. `paused` holds the fill where it is; `onDone` fires when it is full. In RTL the bars fill from the right.

Composed of: [Progress](#progress)

```tsx
<StoryProgress count={items.length} index={$i} run={item.id} paused={$hold} onDone={next} />
```

Full page: src/components/social/story-progress/docs.md

## StoryRing

An Avatar inside a ring that tells the story state: `new` sweeps the four HADİ colors (and pink), `seen` is a quiet line, `close` is the friends-only green, `none` has no ring. As a button it opens the stories, and while they load the ring turns on the motion engine. A `+` badge marks your own ring (add a story); a label under it makes a story tray.

Composed of: [Avatar](#avatar), [CornerMark](#cornermark)

```tsx
<StoryRing name={u.name} src={u.avatar} state={u.seen ? "seen" : "new"} label={u.handle} onClick={() => open(u)} />
```

Full page: src/components/social/story-ring/docs.md

## StoryViewer

Full-screen stories on a dark stage. StoryProgress bars fill on top; a tap on the start third goes back and anywhere else forward (mirrored in RTL); pressing and holding pauses; a horizontal swipe moves to the next or previous person with a slide; dragging down shrinks the story and closes it past 120 px (or a quick flick). The bottom bar has a reply field (typing pauses) and a LikeButton. The next picture is preloaded. It is a Dialog: focus stays inside, Esc closes and focus returns to the ring that opened it.

Composed of: [Dialog](#dialog), [Avatar](#avatar), [StoryProgress](#storyprogress), [LikeButton](#likebutton), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [ListRow](#listrow), [Picture](#picture), [TextInput](#textinput)

```tsx
<StoryViewer open={$open} onClose={() => $open = false} groups={stories} start={tappedId} onSeen={markSeen} onReply={send} />
```

Full page: src/components/composite/story-viewer/docs.md

## Swatch

A sample of a colour or a gradient: the squares of a palette, the presets of a gradient editor, the tones of a theme scale. With `onClick` it is a button that says whether it is selected; without it, a picture. Transparent colours show over a checkerboard.

```tsx
<Swatch color="#ff7a1a" label="Orange" selected={$c === "#ff7a1a"} onClick={() => $c = "#ff7a1a"} />
<Swatch color="linear-gradient(135deg, #ff7a1a, #7c3aed)" shape="circle" size="lg" mark />
<Swatch color="rgb(37 99 235 / .4)" label="Blue, 40%" />
<Swatch color="brand-green" />
<div class={CHECKER} />
```

Full page: src/components/forms/swatch/docs.md

## Tabs

Tabbed panels. Give `tabs` as data or write `<Tab>` children; only the active panel exists (switching disposes the old one). Arrow keys move between tabs with automatic activation, mirrored in RTL. Tabs can carry a count badge, be disabled or hidden, and `query="tab"` keeps the active tab in the URL (`?tab=id`) so a reload or a shared link opens it.

Composed of: [Badge](#badge), [StatusDot](#statusdot)

```tsx
<Tabs value={$tab} onChange={(id) => $tab = id} tabs={[
  { id: "general", label: "General", content: () => <General /> },
  { id: "members", label: "Members", badge: () => $pending, content: () => <Members /> },
]} />
```

Full page: src/components/navigation/tabs/docs.md

## Terminal

An extensible command line in the page — for a playground, a dev console, an admin panel or a product demo.

Composed of: [JsonView](#jsonview), [Window](#window), [Progress](#progress), [Spinner](#spinner)

```tsx
import { Terminal, defineTerminalCommands, ansi } from "hadi-march/components/composite/terminal";

<Terminal prompt="hadi$ " welcome="[info] help yaz" persist="demo" scheme="auto" cursor="block" commands={{
  echo: (a, io) => io.print(a.rest.join(" ")),
  deploy: {
    desc: "Yayınla",
    args: [{ name: "env", required: true, choices: ["staging", "prod"] }],
    options: { force: { alias: "f", desc: "Onay sorma" } },
    run: async (a, io) => {
      const p = io.progress(`${a.args.env} yükleniyor`)
      for (let i = 1; i <= 10; i++) { if (io.signal.aborted) return; await wait(120); p.set(i / 10) }
      p.done(); io.success("Yayında")
    },
  },
  user: { desc: "Kullanıcılar", sub: { list: (_a, io) => io.table(users), add: { args: [{ name: "name", required: true }], run: … } } },
}} ref={(t) => t.exec("help")} />

defineTerminalCommands({ ping: (_a, io) => io.print(ansi.green("pong")) })   // every terminal on the page
```

Full page: src/components/composite/terminal/docs.md

## Testimonials

What customers say, in four layouts: `grid` (quote cards in equal rows), `marquee` (two endless rows drifting at different speeds), `wall` (a masonry wall that fades out, with "Show more") and `slider` (a Carousel). Every card has the quote, an optional star rating, an Avatar, the name and the role.

Composed of: [Card](#card), [Avatar](#avatar), [Rating](#rating), Marquee, [Carousel](#carousel), [Button](#button), [ListRow](#listrow), [Reveal](#reveal)

```tsx
<Testimonials variant="wall" items={[
  { quote: "Our new site was live in a week.", name: "Dana Ray", role: "Head of product, HADİ", rating: 5 },
  …
]} />
```

Full page: src/components/landing/testimonials/docs.md

## TextInput

Single-line text. Works standalone (`bind:value`, `value` + `onChange`, or uncontrolled) and inside a `<Field>` or `<Form>`, which wire its id, `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`. **EmailInput** and **UrlInput** are the same control with the right keyboard, autocomplete and trimming.

```tsx
<Field label="Search"><TextInput bind:value={$q} placeholder="Members, orders…" prefix={<Icon of={search} />} /></Field>
<Field label="E-mail"><EmailInput bind:value={$mail} /></Field>
<Field label="Website"><UrlInput bind:value={$site} /></Field>
```

Full page: src/components/forms/text-input/docs.md

## Textarea

Multi-line text that grows with what is typed (`autosize={false}` keeps the height fixed). Same value and field wiring as TextInput.

```tsx
<Field label="About" help={() => `${$about.length}/280`}><Textarea bind:value={$about} rows={3} maxLength={280} /></Field>
```

Full page: src/components/forms/textarea/docs.md

## ThemeEditor

Make a whole theme and watch it live. Start from a built-in theme (HADİ, Classic Cream, Night Blue, Neon, Indigo, Minimal, High Contrast) or from scratch with one accent color; edit every color token for light and dark with a full ColorPicker (accent, surfaces, text, border, status, HADİ brand colors, the categorical palette), pick tones from an automatic tone scale, and fix contrast with the WCAG audit. Type (font families, scale ratio, line heights, weights), shape (radius scale, spacing, density, shadows, border width) and motion (durations, three easing curves) are tokens too. The preview is a small app screen of real components scoped to the editor (`data-m-theme` + the draft's variables) in light or dark, LTR or RTL, with or without motion; "Apply to the app" switches the whole app to it. Out come the defineTheme module, the stylesheet (themeCss) and JSON; in go pasted JSON, CSS or a share link.

Composed of: [ColorPicker](#colorpicker), [EasingCurveEditor](#easingcurveeditor), [Tabs](#tabs), [Segmented](#segmented), [Slider](#slider), [Select](#select), [TextInput](#textinput), [Textarea](#textarea), [Toggle](#toggle), Field, [Button](#button), [UndoRedo](#undoredo), [CopyButton](#copybutton), [Badge](#badge), [PanelHeader](#panelheader), [SectionLabel](#sectionlabel), [ListRow](#listrow), [Swatch](#swatch), [Stack](#stack), ThemeSwatch, [CodeView](#codeview), [Alert](#alert), [Card](#card), [Checkbox](#checkbox), [Chip](#chip), [Progress](#progress), [Avatar](#avatar)

```tsx
<ThemeEditor />
<ThemeEditor bind:value={$draft} base="night" />
```

Full page: src/components/composite/theme-editor/docs.md

## ThemeMenu

One top-bar menu for the whole look: light / dark / system, the color theme (each drawn by a live swatch of itself) and the accent color. Its sections are the same ones `ThemePicker` and `AccentPicker` show on their own, so an app can use one menu or the separate pickers and they always match. Choices are remembered.

Composed of: Dropdown, ThemeSwatch, [OverflowText](#overflowtext), [SectionLabel](#sectionlabel)

```tsx
<ThemeMenu />
<ThemeMenu themes={false} accents={["primary", "brand-orange", "brand-blue"]} />
<ThemeMenu icon={sun} modes={false} headings={false} />                       // own icon, no light / dark row, no headings
<ThemeMenu icon={false} label="Look" labels={{ theme: "Palette", accent: "Highlight" }} panelClass="my-panel" />
<ThemeMenu view="cards" current modes={false} />     // preview cards of every theme; the button shows the theme in use
```

Full page: src/components/composite/theme-menu/docs.md

## TimeInput

The browser's own time field: the value is `"HH:MM"` (`"HH:MM:SS"` with a step under a minute), in the user's 12- or 24-hour display.

```tsx
<Field label="Start"><TimeInput bind:value={$start} min="09:00" max="18:00" /></Field>
```

Full page: src/components/forms/time-input/docs.md

## TimeRuler

The ruler above a timeline: ticks, time labels and a playhead. Read-only it shows where a run or an animation is. With `onSeek` the ruler is draggable (a press anywhere jumps there) and the playhead becomes a slider. Rows under the ruler use the same scale with `timePercent(ms, duration)`.

```tsx
<TimeRuler duration={2000} value={$now} onSeek={(ms) => playback.seek(ms)} onSeekStart={pause} />
<TimeRuler duration={() => span()} value={() => runner.elapsed()} minor={false} color="brand-orange" />
```

Full page: src/components/data/time-ruler/docs.md

## Timeline

An ordered list of events. Each item has an optional time, title, body, tone (the dot colour) and icon. A `Date`, epoch milliseconds or an ISO string is formatted for the current locale; other text is shown as is.

Composed of: [StatusDot](#statusdot)

```tsx
<Timeline items={[
  { time: "Today 09:12", title: "Order placed", body: "#48210 · 3 items", tone: "info" },
  { time: paidAt, title: "Payment received", tone: "success", icon: check },
]} />
```

Full page: src/components/data/timeline/docs.md

## Toast

Short messages that do not block: `toast(message, { kind, action, timeout })` shows one at the inline end of the bottom edge and returns its id. An action (Undo) is a button inside it; a failing action shows its own error toast. At most five stay on screen. A `<ToastHost />` is mounted on first use when the app has none.

Composed of: Portal, [Alert](#alert), [Button](#button)

```tsx
toast("File archived", { kind: "success", action: { label: "Undo", run: () => restore() } });
```

Full page: src/components/overlays/toast/docs.md

## Toggle

An on / off switch for settings that apply at once. The thumb slides toward the inline end (mirrored in right-to-left pages); the track takes the color token when on.

```tsx
<Toggle bind:value={$notify} label="Instant notifications" />
```

Full page: src/components/forms/toggle/docs.md

## Tooltip

A short hint for the element it wraps. It appears on hover after a short delay and at once on keyboard focus, hides on leave, blur or Esc, and is linked to the element with `aria-describedby`. The popover engine places it and flips it when there is no room.

```tsx
<Tooltip text="Copy link" placement="top"><Button icon={link}>Share</Button></Tooltip>
```

Full page: src/components/overlays/tooltip/docs.md

## Tree

An expandable tree for small hierarchies (file lists, settings sections). Every node can carry an icon and a trailing meta text; long labels scroll with OverflowText instead of ending in an ellipsis. For thousands of nodes, lazy children or drag and drop use TreeView.

Composed of: [ListRow](#listrow), [Chevron](#chevron), [OverflowText](#overflowtext)

```tsx
<Tree label="Files" nodes={files} expanded={["src"]} selected={() => $file} onSelect={(n) => { $file = n.id }} />
```

Full page: src/components/data/tree/docs.md

## TreeEditor

Edit any JSON value as a tree. Each row shows its key, a **type badge** in a HADİ color (objects and lists Heyecan, numbers Aktivite, text Dostluk, true / false İletişim) that converts the value to another type, and the value: a text or number you edit in place, a switch for true / false, a count for objects and lists. Rows add, duplicate and delete; a search box keeps the matches and their parents; a JSON Schema subset marks invalid rows with their message. Every change is one step of the editor's own undo history.

Composed of: [Badge](#badge), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [Toggle](#toggle), [TextInput](#textinput), [SearchBox](#searchbox), [OptionList](#optionlist), [UndoRedo](#undoredo), [Empty](#empty), [EditorFrame](#editorframe), [Popover](#popover)

```tsx
<TreeEditor bind:value={$config} schema={schema} />
<TreeEditor value={data} readonly search={false} expand={1} />
```

Full page: src/components/composite/tree-editor/docs.md

## TreeView

A tree for large hierarchies. Only the rows in view are in the DOM (shared virtual window), so thousands of open nodes stay smooth. Children can load lazily the first time a folder opens, selection is single or multiple, nodes move by drag and drop (before / after / inside, with edge auto-scroll and auto-open of a folder you hover), and search keeps the path to every hit open and highlights the matching text. For a short static tree, `<Tree>` is enough.

Composed of: [ListRow](#listrow), [Chevron](#chevron), [Spinner](#spinner), [Button](#button), [Badge](#badge), [Empty](#empty)

```tsx
import { TreeView } from "hadi-march/components/data/tree-view";

<TreeView nodes={files} selection="multiple" draggable search={$q}
  load={(node) => api.children(node.id)}
  onSelect={(ids) => $selected = ids}
  onMove={(ids, target, position) => api.move(ids, target, position)} />
```

Full page: src/components/data/tree-view/docs.md

## TypingIndicator

Three dots that lift in turn on the motion engine (a staggered loop; still with reduced motion) and an optional sentence: "HADİ is typing…", "HADİ and Beta are typing…", "3 people are typing…". It is a polite status, so screen readers hear the sentence once even when it is not shown. With no names it hides.

Composed of: [StatusDot](#statusdot)

```tsx
<TypingIndicator names={$typing} />
```

Full page: src/components/social/typing-indicator/docs.md

## UndoRedo

The undo / redo pair in the bar of an editor. Give it an undo stack (`undoStack()` / `undoHistory()` of hadi-march/managers/undo) and it follows it: the buttons switch off when there is nothing to undo or redo, and the tooltip names the step and the shortcut ("Undo: Rename (Ctrl+Z)"). Or drive it with four props.

Composed of: [IconButton](#iconbutton)

```tsx
<UndoRedo history={history} />
<UndoRedo canUndo={$past.length > 0} canRedo={$future.length > 0} onUndo={undo} onRedo={redo} size="sm" />
<UndoRedo history={history} actions={["undo"]} shortcuts={false} labels={{ undo: "Step back" }} />
```

Full page: src/components/actions/undo-redo/docs.md

## VerifiedMark

The verified-account badge shown beside a name: a post author, a profile title, a user row. It is an image with an accessible name; the icon, the text, the colour and the size can be changed.

```tsx
<b>{user.name}</b> {user.verified && <VerifiedMark />}
<VerifiedMark size="md" label="Verified organiser" m:color="brand-green" />
<VerifiedMark icon={shieldCheck} label={false} />
```

Full page: src/components/social/verified-mark/docs.md

## VideoBackground

A muted, looping video behind content (a hero, a CTA band, a slide). Built on Overlay: the poster shows first and stays on save-data, 2G and reduced motion; the video plays only while it is visible and is released when it leaves the page. A tint keeps text readable and a small button pauses the motion.

Composed of: [Overlay](#overlay), [IconButton](#iconbutton)

```tsx
<VideoBackground src="/media/clip.webm" poster="/media/clip.jpg" tint="dark">
  <h1>…</h1>
</VideoBackground>
```

Full page: src/components/landing/video-background/docs.md

## VirtualList

A long list that keeps only the rows near the viewport in the DOM, so 100,000 rows scroll like 20. Rows can have any height: each is measured when it renders and an estimate stands in until then; when a row above the viewport changes height the content stays still (scroll anchoring). Rows keep their DOM while they stay in range and receive an accessor to their item, so an updated item (a like, an edit) updates its row instead of rebuilding it.

```tsx
<VirtualList items={$posts} key={(p) => p.id} render={(p) => <PostCard post={p} />} onEndReached={loadMore} />
```

Full page: src/components/data/virtual-list/docs.md

## Window

A window inside its area (the nearest positioned ancestor): move it by the title bar, resize it by an edge or a corner, dock it to half of the area by dropping it on an edge, fill the area, fold it to its title bar, close it. Three looks: `"hadi"` (default), `"mac"` and `"windows"`.

Composed of: [PanelHeader](#panelheader), [IconButton](#iconbutton), [ResizeHandle](#resizehandle)

```tsx
import { Window } from "hadi-march/layout";

<div class="desk">                                   {/* position: relative; any size */}
  <Window title="Notlar" chrome="mac" persist="notes">…</Window>
</div>
```

Full page: src/components/layout/window/docs.md

## Wizard

One form split into steps. Each step shows and validates its own fields (plus an optional `validate` check) before Next; Back keeps what was typed; Finish submits the whole form. The stage list on top is the Steps component: a later stage can be picked once every stage before it passes.

Composed of: [Steps](#steps), [Progress](#progress), [Button](#button), [Alert](#alert)

```tsx
<Wizard submitLabel="Finish" onSubmit={save} steps={[
  { title: "Account", schema: schema({ email: { type: "email", required: true } }) },
  { title: "Profile", schema: schema({ name: { type: "text", required: true } }), validate: (v) => (v.name === "admin" ? "Pick another name" : null) },
]} />
```

Full page: src/components/composite/wizard/docs.md
